articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins plan luxury homes near Tiger Woods' exclusive Mexico golf estate; the Bengals teammates are entering a community with a reported $300,000 joining fee
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are reportedly planning to build homes at Diamante, an exclusive resort community in Cabo
articles.body: Cincinnati Bengals wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are reportedly planning to build homes at Diamante, an exclusive resort community in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. The development is already home to golf legend Tiger Woods, making it an attractive destination for athletes who enjoy golf and luxury living. The move would give both players a place to relax and spend their offseasons away from the demands of professional football.Chase and Higgins Have Visited Diamante for YearsAs reported by Sports Illustrated, Chase and Higgins have been visiting Diamante for around five or six years. Developer Ken Jowdy revealed that the two players have supported the resort for several years and regularly enjoyed its facilities.Building homes there would allow the receivers to spend more time at a destination they already know and appreciate. Rather than making occasional trips during their breaks, they would have their own properties to return to whenever their schedules permit.Located in Cabo San Lucas, Diamante is known for its ocean views, luxury homes and golf facilities. The resort offers a relaxing setting for athletes looking to take a break from training, travel and the pressures of the NFL season.Tiger Woods Has His Own Home at DiamanteThe resort is also home to golf legend Tiger Woods, who has his own property there. The 15-time major champion owns a property at the Legacy Club, an exclusive residential community within Diamante.Woods has also contributed to the resort through his golf course design company, TGR Design. His home is among the first 14 Founder Estates planned for the community and includes personal features such as his corporate logo near the driveway and swimming pool.The Legacy golf course, designed by Woods and Beau Welling, is another major attraction. Its opening has been delayed and is now expected in 2027. Woods has previously designed two other courses at Diamante, strengthening his association with the resort.Membership Costs Around $300,000Joining the Legacy Club requires a financial commitment. Reports place its initial membership fee at approximately $300,000, with annual dues of around $60,000.Membership is limited to 250 families and is available by invitation only. It can also extend to future generations, allowing family members to enjoy the facilities. Along with private golf courses, the community offers luxury residences, ocean views and exclusive amenities.Ja'Marr Chase's Success With CincinnatiChase has become one of the NFL's leading wide receivers since joining the Bengals in 2021. Cincinnati selected him fifth overall in the first round of the NFL Draft following his successful college career at Louisiana State University.He made an impressive start, finishing his rookie season with 1,455 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns. His performances earned him the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year award and helped Cincinnati reach Super Bowl LVI.His 2024 season was another highlight. Chase recorded 127 receptions, 1,708 receiving yards and 17 touchdowns, finishing first in all three categories and winning the receiving Triple Crown. He signed a four-year contract extension with the Bengals in March 2025.Tee Higgins Has Established Himself in CincinnatiHiggins joined the Bengals after being selected in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft. He has developed into an important part of the team's passing attack and a dependable partner for Chase.He recorded more than 1,000 receiving yards in both the 2021 and 2022 seasons. Higgins also continued producing touchdowns, finishing with 10 in 2024 and 11 in 2025. In March 2025, he signed a four-year contract to remain with Cincinnati through the 2028 season.The reported property plans reflect the players' shared interest in golf and their long connection with Diamante. Having homes at the resort would give Chase and Higgins more opportunities to enjoy their time away from football. They would also become neighbours of one of golf's biggest names, Tiger Woods.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sam Darnold injury update: Seahawks keep 49ers guessing ahead of crucial Week 12 showdown
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks are preparing for a crucial Week 12 clash against the San Francisco 49ers, with Sam Darnold's fitness emerging as a key storyline.
articles.body: The Seattle Seahawks are preparing for a crucial Week 12 clash against the San Francisco 49ers, with Sam Darnold's fitness emerging as a key storyline. The quarterback has missed the last two games with quad and rib injuries, but Seattle is hopeful he can return after the bye. Head coach Mike Macdonald has not confirmed Darnold's availability, leaving the 49ers with an important question to answer during their preparations. Seattle enters the matchup with playoff ambitions, and having its starting quarterback back could make a significant difference against a division rival.Sam Darnold's return remains the priority for SeattleDarnold has been the Seahawks' designated starter when healthy, and Macdonald has maintained that position despite Drew Lock winning both games during his absence. The team now needs to see how Darnold responds to the pace of practice before making a final decision.Macdonald offered a cautious update on the quarterback's work during the bye week."He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away. He's optimistic, but I think with today's practice cadence and speed of today, it's probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday's practice," Macdonald said of Darnold's bye week via the team's website.The comments suggest progress, but they stop short of confirming a return. Darnold still has to show he can handle the demands of a full practice without aggravating either injury.Drew Lock also benefits from the bye weekLock has given Seattle a reliable option while Darnold recovers. He helped the Seahawks win their previous two games, making the quarterback decision more complicated than it might have been earlier in the season.However, Lock was also managing an oblique injury before Seattle's previous game against the Las Vegas Raiders. The break gave him time to recover, which could leave the Seahawks with two healthier quarterbacks heading into the 49ers matchup."I'd say the bye week was really helpful for Drew," Macdonald said via the team's website. "A really well-deserved chance for him to feel better, and that's going to help us moving forward. I think that's the case for several of our guys as well."Seahawks could force 49ers to prepare for both quarterbacksSeattle has little reason to rush an announcement before Darnold completes the next stage of his recovery. If he avoids a setback and handles the practice workload, he is expected to reclaim the starting job.Keeping the decision open also creates a practical challenge for San Francisco. The 49ers must prepare for Darnold's return while accounting for Lock, who has already shown he can lead the offense to wins.The Seahawks and 49ers are scheduled to kick off at 1:25 pm PT on Sunday at Levi's Stadium. The game will air on FOX and stream on the FOX One app.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Power Ranking The NFL's Top Executives After 49ers Extend GM John Lynch
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season is seemingly shaping up to be a special one for the San Francisco 49ers. While their depth has been tested by injuries, they are tied for the league's best record and have looked like the NFL's clear-cut top team more often than not.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is seemingly shaping up to be a special one for the San Francisco 49ers. While their depth has been tested by injuries, they are tied for the league's best record and have looked like the NFL's clear-cut top team more often than not.

Sunday night's dismantling of the Minnesota Vikings' vaunted defense certainly cemented San Francisco as the team to beat in the NFC.

General manager John Lynch has done an excellent job of building this 49ers team. According to Fox Sports insider Jay Glazer , Lynch was rewarded with a multi-year extension shortly before Sunday's game took place.

While the timing of the deal may be curious, Jed York's decision to extend Lynch is not. He's become one of the top executives in the league over the past decade and may have San Francisco on the cusp of another Super Bowl.

Where does Lynch rank among the league's very best? Let's dive into the resumes, the recent results, and the savviest moves, and rank the top 10 execs in the NFL today.

George Paton has only been in charge of the Denver Broncos since 2021, and he made one of recent history's biggest mistakes when he acquired and extended quarterback Russell Wilson.

Adding Wilson cost Denver two first-round picks, two second-round picks, and more. Extending him required a five-year, $245 million agreement. Wilson lasted just two seasons before he was dumped.

Since the Wilson debacle, though, Paton and head coach Sean Payton have constructed one of the league's most complete rosters. They've found a high-level starter in Bo Nix and have forged a defense that currently ranks 11th in points allowed. Had Nix not suffered a fractured ankle in the playoffs last season, the Broncos may well have reached Super Bowl LX.

While Paton's drafts have been inconsistent—and he may have whiffed on the Jaylen Waddle trade—he's done a great job of finding and extending young centerpiece players like Patrick Surtain II, Nik Bonitto, and Riley Moss.

Brian Gutekunst has been in the Green Bay Packers' front office since 1999, and he worked his way from being a scout to the general manager over the course of nearly two decades.

Since Gutekunst took over his current role in 2018, the Packers have largely operated with a draft-and-develop philosophy. It has worked extremely well recently, as Green Bay has been a consistent contender with one of the NFL's youngest rosters since Jordan Love took over at quarterback.

Setting up the succession plan for Aaron Rodgers was also a masterful move by Gutekunst. Trading up for Love seemed like an odd move in 2020, but the Packers are now on the upswing while Rodgers is finishing out his career with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Has everything gone smoothly during Gutekunst's tenure? Of course not. Last year's blockbuster trade for Micah Parsons currently grades as an incomplete due to his ACL injury, and Green Bay has struggled to rebuild its offensive line.

The Packers have also won just three postseason games in eight full seasons with Gutekunst at the helm. Of course, they've also made the playoffs six times in that span.

Lynch became San Francisco's president of football operations in 2023, but he's been the GM since 2017—the same year in which head coach Kyle Shanahan was hired. Since 2017, the 49ers have appeared in four NFC title games and two Super Bowls.

Now, it's worth noting that Lynch and Shanahan make many of the team's roster decisions together.

"What Kyle and I have talked about from Day 1 is that this needs to be a partnership," Lynch said after he was hired, per the team's official website .

The 49ers have also had some misses under Lynch. The 2017 trade for Jimmy Garoppolo helped get San Francisco to the Super Bowl. "Finding" Brock Purdy in the seventh round of the 2022 draft set up the franchise for the future. However, if we're going to credit Lynch for those moves, we must also hold him accountable for the Trey Lance fiasco.

For anyone who forgot, the 49ers traded three first-round picks and a third-rounder to move up and snag Lance in the 2021 draft. He went on to start just four games for San Francisco.

Still, Lynch has helped construct a perennial contender and what might be this year's most talented and deepest roster. This year alone, he added the likes of Mike Evans, Dre Greenlaw, Kaelon Black, Keenan Allen, and DeForest Buckner.

1 Thing Every NFL Fanbase Should Be Thankful For 🙏

Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles only ranks this low because he's been in the job for just four full years. His work during that stretch, though, has been enviable.

Poles inherited a middling roster and a cache of 2022 draft picks that didn't include a first-round pick because of the previous year's trade to land Justin Fields. Since then, he has made a series of brilliant moves that have helped create one of the league's most competitive rosters.

In 2023, Poles traded the No. 1 overall pick in the draft for a hefty haul from the Carolina Panthers. The following year, he made the "safe" choice by taking quarterback Caleb Williams No. 1 overall. Last offseason, he and the Bears lured Ben Johnson away from the rival Detroit Lions to be their head coach. At this year's trade deadline, he snagged Jeffery Simmons away from the Tennessee Titans for a pair of first-round picks and a fifth-rounder.

Along the way, Poles has uncovered promising young players like Colston Loveland, Luther Burden III, Darnell Wright, and Kyle Monangai.

We'll have to see how Poles' moves age over time, but he and Johnson could have the Bears soon headed to their first Super Bowl since the 2006 season.

Did Jason Licht make a mistake by giving quarterback Baker Mayfield a three-year, $165 million extension before the start of this season? Perhaps, but Licht also brought in Mayfield and constructed a team capable of contending in the post-Tom Brady era.

Of course, Licht also brought in Brady, Rob Gronkowski, Tristan Wirfs, Leonard Fournette, Antoine Winfield Jr. and the rest of the roster that won the Super Bowl in 2020. His first draft choice as Tampa's general manager was future Hall of Famer and current 49ers star Mike Evans.

While Licht will probably be remembered for giving Brady his second act, he doesn't get nearly enough credit for what came after. Head coach Bruce Arians stepped down after the 2021 season, and Brady retired after the 2022 campaign. Yet, the Bucs stayed at the top of the NFC South for both 2023 and 2024.

Injuries caused Tampa to narrowly miss out on another division title last year, and the team is currently in a 3-7 slump. However, this year's team is 2-0 in divisional play and still has a shot to storm back into the playoff picture.

The Bucs have gone from being stuck in the NFC South basement to being consistently relevant in the division under Licht's guidance.

Head coach Dan Campbell has gotten a ton of credit for taking one of the NFL's most snake-bitten franchises and turning it into a perennial playoff contender. However, GM Brad Holmes deserves just as much credit, if not more.

Holmes' first big decision as the Lions' general manager was a doozy. He traded star quarterback Matthew Stafford to the Los Angeles Rams for a pair of first-round picks, a third-round pick, and quarterback Jared Goff. It couldn't have been an easy choice, given how much Stafford had meant to the franchise.

However, it proved to be a smart choice, and Holmes has made many more since. Stafford immediately won a Super Bowl with the Rams, but Holmes used Goff and that extra draft capital to build a rock-solid foundation.

Over the past half-decade, Holmes has been one of the league's best at finding, drafting, and extending talent. Penei Sewell, Aidan Hutchinson, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jahmyr Gibbs, Jack Campbell, Sam LaPorta, Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph, and Jameson Williams were all drafted under Holmes' watch.

There is some recency bias involved in this ranking, as the Rams didn't really find sustained success until they hired head coach Sean McVay in 2017. Of course, Snead played a big role in the difficult decision to hire a 30-year-old McVay then.

Team president Kevin Demoff and senior assistant Tony Pastoors were also part of the process. However, according to ESPN's Aidan Gonzalez , it was Snead who "told the room that he hoped they all had the courage to do the right thing."

Snead and McVay have largely worked together on personnel decisions since then, and Snead is probably best-known for his "F them picks" philosophy. However, he's done a lot more than bring in a brilliant coach and play real-life fantasy football.

Yes, McVay and high-profile trade acquisitions like Matthew Stafford, Von Miller, Myles Garrett, and Trent McDuffie will be lasting pieces of Snead's legacy.

Stafford and Miller helped the Rams win the Super Bowl following the 2021 season, while later additions Garrett and McDuffie have bolstered their pursuit of another title in 2026.

However, Snead also took Aaron Donald 13th overall in 2014 and has regularly hit home runs with late-round picks in recent years. Puka Nacua, Kyren Williams, Kobie Turner, Byron Young, and Quentin Lake are current key contributors who were all drafted in the third round or later.

Brett Veach wasn't the Chiefs' general manager when they drafted Patrick Mahomes, but he played an integral role in scouting him before succeeding John Dorsey.

However, Veach has done a tremendous job of putting competitive rosters around Mahomes and building a dynasty in Kansas City. Since Mahomes became the starter in 2018, the Chiefs have made seven AFC title games, reached five Super Bowls, won three Lombardi Trophies, and missed the playoffs only once.

Yes, having Mahomes and head coach Andy Reid has made it easier to build a perennial contender. However, Veach has added players like Trey Smith, Trent McDuffie, L'Jarius Sneed, and Rashee Rice while financially managing a championship-caliber roster.

Veach has done a masterful job of knowing when to pay players, when not to pay players, and when to flip veterans like McDuffie and Tyreek Hill for draft capital. Super Bowl teams are never easy to keep together. However, the Chiefs have consistently juggled cap dollars and back-filled positions with rookie contracts while maintaining one of the AFC's top rosters.

While Kansas City did experience a down year in 2025, it's right back in the Super Bowl mix this year thanks to recent additions like Mansoor Delane, Cyrus Allen, Kenneth Walker III, and Josh Downs.

It's nearly impossible to overstate just how important John Schneider has been to the Seattle Seahawks franchise.

The current president of football operations (since 2024) first became the general manager in 2010. Since then, he has overseen two distinct eras that have resulted in Super Bowl championships.

Schneider drafted Russell Wilson in 2012 and helped assemble the Legion of Boom defense, which included draft selections such as Richard Sherman, Kam Chancellor, Earl Thomas, Bobby Wagner and K.J. Wright. Along with head coach Pete Carroll, that group reached two Super Bowls and won one.

When Carroll was moved into an advisory role in 2024, Schneider hired head coach Mike Macdonald, who led Seattle to a Super Bowl title in his second season. The 2025 championship roster was littered with more draft gems such as Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Devon Witherspoon, Charles Cross, Byron Murphy II, Nick Emmanwori, and Kenneth Walker III.

Between the two eras, Schneider orchestrated the trade that sent Wilson to Denver and laid the foundation for a roster overhaul. Last offseason, he replaced Geno Smith with Sam Darnold to provide a higher ceiling at quarterback.

In all, Seattle has made the playoffs 11 times in the 16 seasons since Schneider was hired.

Parallels exist between Schneider and Philadelphia Eagles executive vice president Howie Roseman. Both were hired as GMs in 2010, and both have overseen multiple Super Bowl eras since. Both have also seen their teams reach three Super Bowls with two victories.

Both Schneider and Roseman are likely headed to the Hall of Fame, too.

What puts Roseman in our top spot is his ability to field competitive teams despite turnover at quarterback and head coach. He saw the end of the Andy Reid era and survived the forgettable Chip Kelly era. He watched Nick Foles and Doug Pederson beat Tom Brady and Bill Belichick in the big game. He crafted a team that has been a perennial contender with Jalen Hurts and Nick Sirianni—at least, when healthy.

Roseman has masterfully conducted drafts and managed the cap, and he has an uncanny knack for making shrewd business decisions and coming out ahead.

Consider the fact that Roseman traded first- and third-round picks for A.J. Brown in 2022. The Eagles got four years and a Lombardi Trophy out of Brown, then flipped him to the New England Patriots for first- and fifth-round draft picks. He drafted Jordan Davis in the first round in 2022 and just traded him for first- and second-round picks after four years of service.

The Eagles have made 10 playoff appearances under Roseman's guidance with seven NFC East titles. This is a down year for them because of injuries, but they're set up nicely for the next few years because of Roseman's NFL business brilliance.

articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 12 2026 NFL Picks
articles.summary: A 16-game slate is on the menu for the holiday week. Will Bleacher Report's expert crew feast on Week 12 spreads?
articles.body:
A 16-game slate is on the menu for the holiday week. Will Bleacher Report's expert crew feast on Week 12 spreads?

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , mostly handled the previous week's big spreads well. In Week 12, they had to break down several marquee matchups with tighter spreads. Four of the five games between Wednesday and Friday have spreads of a field goal or less.

We could see a good number of nail-biters this week, but the panelists will help you read between the lines for some wins. First, check out the standings below.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Green Bay Packers (6-4) at Los Angeles Rams (6-4)

Sean McVay has never beaten Matt LaFleur, and I don't see that changing here. Micah Parsons should be back for Green Bay, giving an already good defense a significant boost.

The Rams run the ball well and have righted the ship after a slow start to the season, but the Packers should be able to slow down the run without having to worry about Puka Nacua or Davante Adams through the air. Jordan Love stays hot as the Packers get a big win in the NFC playoff race.

Of all the meaningful Thanksgiving holiday early-week matchups — and there are five of 'em — this Wednesday night Week 12 opener may be the most important on the plate. The Rams and Packers are both reeling in different ways, both coming off the bye and both in danger of playing their way out of playoff contention.

Los Angeles has battled injuries, inconsistency and overhyped expectations all season. It's time for the defense, the pass rush specifically, to wake up and take over a game. If not now, against a Packers team that surrendered eight sacks and 12 QB hits the last time it took the field, then when? A back-and-forth game ends with the Rams defense on the field preserving a field-goal-or-greater lead.

Packers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton

Chicago Bears (8-2) at Detroit Lions (8-2)

The Lions have been playing on Thanksgiving since 1934. In Motown, they're as much a holiday tradition as cranberry sauce that still bears the ridges of the can.

But this year's game carries massive stakes: The winner will be alone in first place in the NFL's best division. Detroit is at home on a short week. The Bears lean heavily on a running game the Lions should be able to contain. And Detroit's offense can score on anyone.

This should be an NFC North thriller, though the healthier Bears are the safe bet. The Lions have beaten the Miami Dolphins, New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers by 10 or more points on their three-game winning streak, but Chicago fields a more potent offense than any of those teams.

Without All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell and two-time Pro Bowl edge-rusher Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions won't be able to slow down the Bears' eighth-ranked scoring offense. Chicago wins a high-scoring game by at least a field goal.

Lions: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Sobleski

Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) at Dallas Cowboys (5-6)

The Cowboys won the first matchup between these two teams easily and are flying on offense right now, but I'm taking the points. A healthy Saquon Barkley should help the Eagles control the tempo of this one a bit, and the Philadelphia defense showed some mettle in Week 11 with a big win over the Steelers. The Eagles won't win this one, but it's much closer than it was the last time around.

At first blush, this feels like far too big a line for an NFC East matchup. The Eagles have done a respectable job of enduring injuries and got their first win with quarterback Joe Milton III in Week 11. The Cowboys' defense, meanwhile, remains terrible.

However, the Cowboys' offense has been spectacular over the last couple of weeks, and the Eagles just don't have the same playoff-caliber defense that they've had in recent years. And, while the Cowboys are bad defensively, they should have a sound plan to attack Milton on a short week.

Dallas won the first meeting by three scores. While a healthy Saquon Barkley should make the rematch more competitive, I still think the Cowboys will find a way to pull away on Thanksgiving.

Eagles: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton

Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at Buffalo Bills (9-1)

Both teams have steamrolled their last three opponents, but the Chiefs actually have the edge over Buffalo in terms of expected W-L and point differential.

The Bills offense has looked far from crisp lately, and the defense could come crashing back to earth against a quality opponent—especially with Christian Benford, Dorian Williams, Greg Rousseau and Ed Oliver all hurting.

Put simply, I'm slightly less convinced the Bills are as good as their record suggests.

Suddenly, the Bills are playing defense and that should scare anyone. They have been dominant lately, forcing nine turnovers in the last four games and allowing fewer than 200 yards in three of those contests.

Josh Allen has been a bit up and down recently, but I expect the Buffalo QB to bring it in what might be a preview of the AFC Championship. With Kenneth Walker III possibly on the shelf again, the Bills get a huge win behind a big day from Josh Allen and James Cook.

Bills: Davenport, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

Denver Broncos (8-2) at Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4)

The Steelers have not looked great since the bye—a two-week slump summed up by DK Metcalf getting ejected. Pittsburgh needs a spark, but that's not the kind anyone had in mind.

Still, the 6-4 Steelers are at home, with a packed house and a national TV spotlight Friday. Denver's offense has been inconsistent, to put it kindly. Take the points with Pittsburgh. Stop me if you've heard that before.

The Steelers are 4-0 ATS at home this season, but I think that ends here. Pittsburgh's offense has looked toothless two weeks in a row and suffered two bad losses because of it.

The defense has also taken a step back and while I don't see Bo Nix as someone to exploit that, I do think Jonah Coleman turns in another productive day on the ground as his dark-horse OROY campaign starts to take shape. The Steelers have fallen back to Earth hard after a good start, and I think we see them take yet another step back here.

Broncos: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

New Orleans Saints (3-7) at Cincinnati Bengals (7-3)

The Bengals will be coming in on a short week, but I think the offense will be eager to get back on track after struggling against the Commanders on MNF. New Orleans can't run the ball at all offensively, and being one-dimensional through the air sounds like a recipe for getting the ball back in Joe Burrow's hands quickly and often.

The Saints have hung tough this season even in games they've lost, but I think the Bengals bounce back with a dominant win to stay among the AFC's top contenders.

I felt a lot better about making this pick before the Bengals fell flat on Monday Night Football . The Saints are now likely to see an angry Joe Burrow on Sunday, which could be a massive problem.

To be fair, I don't think New Orleans will upset Cincinnati the way that Washington did. However, this is too large of a line for a Bengals squad that had largely beaten up on suspect teams over the past month. I can't ignore the fact that Cincinnati only beat Miami by a touchdown, went to overtime with the Titans, and lost to Pittsburgh this season.

Is New Orleans a bad team? Maybe, but I'll still take the points here. The Saints' defense, while not exactly good, has been better since the bye, and it managed to keep things within striking distance against the Bears. I think we'll see a similar outcome in Cincinnati.

Saints: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Baltimore Ravens (4-7) at Houston Texans (4-6)

This is it. This is the breaking point for the 2026 Ravens. Last week's loss in Carolina ended any realistic playoff hopes—hopes that had already faded when Lamar Jackson landed on injured reserve.

Houston's chances of pulling off another late run to a playoff spot after another dismal start aren't great—you can only buck the odds so many times. But the Texans have won two of three since the bye by an average of 22.5 points and had a 17-point lead in their loss.

The Texans' defense looked terrific last Thursday night, though it was facing a struggling Indianapolis offense. We're likely to see a return to the mean for Houston's defense in Week 12, which will mean largely average play.

Largely average is likely the ceiling for the Ravens without Lamar Jackson. Baltimore looked much better offensively in its second game with placeholder Jacoby Brissett last week, but the defense is still suspect. Brissett and Co. dropped 33 points on the Carolina Panthers last week but surrendered 35 points while turning the ball over four times.

A cleaner game here could allow Baltimore to pull off the outright upset. I expect a surprisingly entertaining game between sub-.500 teams, one that comes down to a late score and a slim margin.

New York Giants (6-3-1) at Indianapolis Colts (3-8)

The Colts are not good, but they've been outscored by just six total points in their last four home games, while the Giants have a negative road scoring margin this season.

Indianapolis has had extra time to prepare for the Giants, a young team that could easily fall into a road trap between home matchups with the Jaguars and 49ers.

Put it all together, and I'm definitely taking the points.

I'm taking the points here, though my Giants picks seem to go wrong whichever side I choose. Big Blue rarely finds itself favored on the road.

Since 2020 , the Giants have been road favorites just four times, going 2-2 against the spread. That's a remarkably small number over nearly seven seasons.

I'm willing to back Big Blue in this road game, featuring a defense that is starting to come into its own, against a Colts offense turning to Anthony Richardson at QB after the outright release of Daniel Jones this past week.

The Giants tend to play up and down to competition—typically a sign of a football team that isn't legitimately good. I'm asking to be hurt here, and I know it, but I hope the Giants prove me wrong once and for all.

Giants: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

New York Jets (3-8) at Miami Dolphins (1-9)

The Dolphins defense actually played quite well in Buffalo. This team fights for this staff, and it beat the Jets on the road just a month ago. Gang Green hasn't won back-to-back road games since 2023, so I'll take that field goal plus a hook all day.

The Jets took an embarrassing Week 7 loss to the then-winless Dolphins. In that game, Geno Smith threw for 287 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. He's coming off a three-touchdown passing performance in Los Angeles. Smith has a hot hand, should be confident against a familiar opponent, and grew up in South Florida.

Dynamic quarterback Malik Willis, who threw for two touchdowns and scored on a rushing touchdown in the first meeting between these teams, is on injured reserve. Meanwhile, Miami will start second-year quarterback Kyle McCord for a third consecutive game. He hasn't thrown a touchdown pass yet.

The Jets avenge their loss to the Dolphins and cover the hook.

Jets: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Tennessee Titans (1-9) at Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3)

This pick gives me pre-Thanksgiving indigestion.

The Jaguars have been better at home than on the road. They are also probably quite angry after last week's listless loss in New York. But the Tennessee offense has shown some life. The Jaguars secondary might be a problem. And this spread leaves the back door wide open.

There's always a pause before taking heavy favorites, but you can feel somewhat comfortable laying just under two touchdowns with the Jaguars against the Titans, given that they covered this line in Tennessee two weeks ago.

Yes, the Jaguars stumbled on the road against the New York Giants last week, but they have won three of their five home games by at least 24 points. By the way, the Titans have allowed 40-plus points in three consecutive contests. Jacksonville flexes against a defense that's giving up a ton of points lately.

Jaguars: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Atlanta Falcons (3-7) at Minnesota Vikings (7-3)

The dismantling of the Vikings' vaunted defense we saw on Sunday night won't soon be forgotten. The Falcons certainly paid attention, and they've had two weeks to come up with a game plan to attack Brian Flores' unit.

The problem for Atlanta is that it doesn't have Brock Purdy behind center—few teams do. San Francisco found success because Purdy was repeatedly able to beat the blitz. Michael Penix Jr. simply lacks the experience and pocket presence needed to emulate Purdy's performance.

While Minnesota's offense struggled mightily in the loss to San Francisco, it is better with Kirk Cousins behind center than it was before his arrival. I expect Cousins to open things up against Atlanta's 29th-ranked defense and for the Vikings to hand the Falcons their fourth straight loss in fairly comfortable fashion.

Everyone has learned a few things about the Vikings in recent weeks. If an opponent can run the ball, Brian Flores' defense is not nearly as effective. In fact, Minnesota ranks 15th in run defense.

Enter Bijan Robinson. Now, Michael Penix Jr. isn't capable of getting the ball out as quickly and accurately as Brock Purdy did this past weekend, but the Falcons did have two weeks to game plan for this contest, which should help them be completely prepared for what they're about to face.

Falcons: Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

New England Patriots (5-5) at Los Angeles Chargers (1-9)

The Patriots have been hammered in back-to-back games, and before that they barely beat the Dolphins.

I can just see their season falling apart without Drake Maye, while the Chargers have begun to get their groove back offensively and don't seem to be giving up on their season.

That said, considering Justin Herbert's status in concussion protocol, I wouldn't spend any money either way on this one.

Tommy DeVito doesn't need to be the next Tom Brady here. He's had two weeks to prepare for a one-win Chargers team that enters Week 12 with the third-fewest points scored.

Even if DeVito is mediocre, it won't take much for the Patriots to outscore the Chargers in a coin-flip game. New England helps him with the ground game; Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner lead New England to a gritty road win off a bye week.

Chargers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Seattle Seahawks (6-4) at San Francisco 49ers (9-1)

I had to double-check, but I was right: I've picked the 49ers 10 of 11 weeks so far this season. The lone week against San Francisco was the Falcons game, which the 49ers lost.

Safe to say I've got a bead on this team, or at least I trust the best team in the NFL the most to win, lose or not cover pretty strongly. I'm not going to stop picking them now.

Seattle lost the first meeting with San Francisco by only three points. The Seahawks have also had two weeks to prepare for the rematch.

Plus, the Seahawks should be getting quarterback Sam Darnold, left tackle Charles Cross and defensive tackle Leonard Williams back in the lineup. The Niners may be rolling, but legitimate rivalry games, when it's good-on-good, tend to be close contests that could go either way.

49ers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Washington Commanders (4-5-1) at Arizona Cardinals (3-8)

This isn't an overreaction to the Washington Commanders' Monday night upset win over the Cincinnati Bengals. The Arizona Cardinals haven't scored more than seven points in three straight games, with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck and 40-year-old Josh Johnson as their starting quarterbacks.

The Cardinals have the league's worst quarterback situation and one reliable pass-catcher, tight end Trey McBride. Eyeing their third consecutive victory, the Commanders see an opening in the NFC East title race. Washington continues to roll as rookie wideout Antonio Williams blossoms into a playmaker.

I picked the Cards before Washington sprung the surprise upset over Cincinnati this past Monday night. I could make a change, but I don't trust Washington to string together many strong performances.

The Commanders are competent and/or efficient in a lot of areas, but winning three in a row is tough for a team that basically plays for possession, to not turn the ball over, and flies by the seat of its pants—or its QB's mobility—for the majority of its playmaking.

The Cardinals, meanwhile, have scored 16 points total over the last three games. That's 5.3 points per game. Time for an anomaly. Give me the points.

Commanders: Davenport, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) at Cleveland Browns (6-4)

The Las Vegas Raiders have lost three straight and seven of their last eight, but Fernando Mendoza looks ready for the prime-time spotlight. Without All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, the rookie quarterback threw for 267 yards, three touchdowns and an interception against the Denver Broncos last week.

Bowers logged limited practice time last Thursday and Friday, making it likely he'll suit up for Sunday Night Football . Mendoza could lead the Raiders to an outright win with his best playmaker.

Keep in mind the Cleveland Browns are averaging 18.8 points per game. The Raiders averaged 18.5 points in Mendoza's first two starts. This is a field-goal game either way.

At this point, where there's a will, there's a way. The Browns are seemingly finding ways to will themselves toward unexpected victories. With this particular matchup, the advantage should be given to Cleveland's defense, which has consistently made life difficult on opposing offenses. In his third start, Fernando Mendoza is about to face the league's sixth-best pass defense. Mistakes are bound to happen.

Raiders: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Carolina Panthers (5-5) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7)

The Bucs have more than a half-victory advantage over Carolina in terms of expected W-L, and they have a positive scoring margin while the Panthers do not.

The Panthers generally lack the talent to string together three wins in a row, and you just know nobody is about to run away with this division.

Tampa Bay crushed Carolina by 30 points on the road a month ago and should win by at least three points in prime time.

The Buccaneers are favored in this game? Tampa is 1-4 ATS at home this season. They shouldn't be laying anything here. This should be a genuine pick 'em.

Even if Carolina doesn't earn the W, this game will be decided by some silly final-possession scenario, so I will take the points as the NFC South hangs in the balance.

A Panthers win would significantly widen the gap in the NFL's bottom-dwelling division.

Panthers: Davenport, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Buccaneers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton

articles.title: Re-Drafting Simon Edvinsson and the Top 10 Picks From the 2021 NHL Draft
articles.summary: We've all seen the discourse stirred up by Simon Edvinsson's trade request. But the situation has also raised another question: How would we re-draft the 2021 NHL class today?
articles.body:
We've all seen the discourse stirred up by Simon Edvinsson's trade request . But the situation has also raised another question: How would we re-draft the 2021 NHL class today?

With a re-draft, you're not selecting solely on skill set; you're factoring in team needs as well. Still, sometimes a team is better served by taking the best player available than by filling a specific roster hole that fans or front-office staff may fixate on.

We also have the significant benefit of more than five years of hindsight, including what we've seen this season, with players developing in different leagues and at different levels along the way.

Even so, one player often rises to the top in a re-draft, and the 2021 class is no different.

1. Buffalo Sabres: Wyatt Johnston, Center

There was no other choice for our re-drafted first overall pick than current Dallas Stars center Wyatt Johnston.

The Buffalo Sabres initially selected a defenseman (Owen Power, still a member of the team), but were not in a place in 2021 to turn down a highly skilled center, either.

Johnston being the standout of the class became apparent so quickly after he made his NHL debut. More importantly, that has remained true over the years since.

If we're looking solely at points scored, Johnston tops the list of 2021 drafted players easily with 283 points in 348 games. He also easily clears the points-per-game list with 0.813. So why wasn't he picked first overall at the time? He missed his entire draft season in the OHL. It's hard to get a good read on a guy when you only see him in seven tournament games.

Would drafting Wyatt Johnston have single-handedly fixed all of the Buffalo Sabres' problems? Of course not, but it's hard to deny that it would have given them a much-needed boost at the time.

2. Seattle Kraken: Matty Beniers, Center

Much like it's difficult to argue against drafting Johnston first overall, it's also difficult to find a convincing argument for pulling center Matty Beniers out of the second overall slot.

The Seattle Kraken have underperformed in the intervening years, but their lack of success does not negate the fact that Beniers is a highly skilled and reliable player.

There are other players you could make an argument for picking in this spot; Beniers kicked off a drafting trend of the Kraken taking many centers, and it's an interesting thought to consider what might have changed if they'd taken a defenseman, for example.

The next few players on this list fall into a similar tier, talent-wise. Defenseman Simon Edvinsson and winger Matthew Knies are both excellent picks in a vacuum, and if this were a ranking, they might jump Beniers on the list.

But because it's a re-draft, as a tiebreaker, consider who you'd pick if you were building a team from scratch, knowing that this is only your first pick.

My gut says Beniers because he's a solid, defensively gifted center with more scoring capability than we've seen in our universe, so here we are. It's a foundation that should've been built differently than it has.

3. Anaheim Ducks: Simon Edvinsson, Defenseman

Ah, the man who started the conversation. Let's get this out of the way: Simon Edvinsson's trade request is not a product of him thinking too highly of himself.

He is highly skilled. One of the foundations of his game was creative, extremely active playmaking. Because he was young and had the puck a lot, that didn't just show up as high-event; it showed up as high-mistake. It happens.

With time, though, Edvinsson has refined his game, growing into his skill set and adapting to his opponents. His decision-making has improved as he's shed many of his less-effective on-ice tendencies, becoming a player who contributes at both ends of the ice.

If the Detroit Red Wings weren't completely going through it, they'd have a great defenseman on their hands. In this universe it's the Anaheim Ducks who have that blessing, and who would've ended up taking defensemen with both of their highest picks that year (the other being Olen Zellweger, who would eventually be traded to the Buffalo Sabres).

Whoever gets him in our world at the end of the day has a mobile, agile, two-way defender coming their way.

4. New Jersey Devils: Matthew Knies, Left Wing

Left wing Matthew Knies would've served the New Jersey Devils far better than defenseman Luke Hughes overall, but particularly at fourth overall.

Since the Toronto Maple Leafs traded him the day before the season opened, Knies has scored 14 points in 21 games with the Columbus Blue Jackets, including a recent key goal against the Leafs.

He's definitely more someone who is going to complement elite players better than driving play himself, which is why he's the perfect choice here.

Imagine Knies with Jack Hughes. Imagine Knies with Nico Hischier. He's very good at anticipating what his linemates are going to be doing and where they'll be, and he's an excellent playmaker and puck retriever.

The thought of pairing his skill set with either one of theirs is extremely appealing, and frankly would've given the team much more of a boost than Luke Hughes on defense.

Hughes is one of those players I got wrong in his draft year. I overrated his abilities and how they would transfer to the NHL, but I wasn't the only one. Knies, conversely, was underrated by many people in both the public and team spheres.

5. Columbus Blue Jackets: Dylan Guenther, Right Wing

Zero shade whatsoever to Kent Johnson, who is still a solid NHLer and has just been passed by other players from the 2021 class, but Dylan Guenther has really surprised me.

At the time of his draft year, I knew he'd be valuable, but I did not necessarily expect him to be so consistent and durable. The guys ahead of him on this list are only there by virtue of their individual skill sets being less easy to acquire elsewhere and better for the teams in question.

There are arguments to be made for Guenther to jump higher on this list.

In this universe where he is selected by the Columbus Blue Jackets, it is a no-brainer to say that his consistency and durability would've served the Blue Jackets better than Kent Johnson.

His game hasn't really changed much since his WHL days, but the key is that it hasn't needed to. He's found success by sticking to what he's good at. And what he's good at is keeping it simple, getting to the net and finding good shooting opportunities on offense, and ensuring he is in the right spot to shut down opportunities on defense.

6. Detroit Red Wings: William Eklund, Left Wing

While his development was a slower one than some other players on this list, left wing William Eklund—traded in days before the NHL Draft in June from the San Jose Sharks to the Ottawa Senators, though he's currently out with a serious ankle injury—has definitely turned out to bring first-round value every time that he steps onto the ice.

He did that by refining areas of his game that were already strengths and addressing weaknesses (his skating, for example).

What would his career look like now if the Detroit Red Wings had drafted him instead of defenseman Simon Edvinsson? Would Eklund be the player asking for a trade now, or would he have managed to find a place to fit?

The Red Wings take prospect development slower (when they do it), so perhaps the longer runway Eklund required would've been a better fit here. His intelligence is nothing to sneeze at, and he's a great playmaker.

He might not evade defenders the way that we hoped in his draft year, but he's found ways to use his hockey sense to drive play and minimize how much of a concern that lack of manipulation can be.

7. San Jose Sharks: Owen Power, Defenseman

With Eklund already off the list, this pick was an intriguing puzzle piece to try to select. The middle of this top 10 feels more like a tier than a strict ranking in terms of talent, so this pick leans on fit and team needs.

Selecting Owen Power, the real-life first overall, was a no-brainer when looking through that lens.

Power is such a reliable defender that a team can grow around him. He's been outpaced by some others in this draft class, but the last few seasons have seen growth in his ability to impose his will on the flow of the game, drive play at a high level, and develop his anticipation even further.

Everyone wants a defenseman they can utilize like a forward until they actually try to do so. Power is a player you can take that opportunity with in certain situations and not worry as much about the outcome.

It's fascinating to imagine what the San Jose Sharks' rebuild would look like right now if they'd gotten Power instead of Eklund.

It's not that Power is a better player, but he fills a very different kind of role. How different would things be if they'd acquired Power in 2021, three years before selecting Sam Dickinson?

8. Los Angeles Kings: Mason McTavish, Center

While he wasn't as much of a reach as some high picks, Mason McTavish was probably not third-overall material even at the time.

Anywhere from about eight to 13 seems fair in a vacuum. When we're taking team needs into consideration, it's an interesting mindset shift to take the Los Angeles Kings from selecting a defenseman to selecting a center. They obviously fill very different needs, but every team needs more centers (unless you're the Seattle Kraken).

McTavish hasn't quite lived up to his draft hype, and two of the questions I had at the time remain: Would his playmaking translate to the NHL, and could he become a strong, pesky checking presence? So far, the answer to both has been closer to no than yes.

Still, he's an effective player who hasn't quite established his identity. Perhaps a different team and development environment would have pushed him to identify and use his strengths sooner.

9. Arizona Coyotes: Brandt Clarke, Defenseman

The Arizona Coyotes, whose roster and hockey operations were transferred to the franchise now known as the Utah Mammoth, initially selected Dylan Guenther with this pick. He's long gone off the board. Who to select?

Brandt Clarke is such an interesting and intelligent player, and it's easy to see that, given the state of the Coyotes at the time, he would've played more NHL games, more consistently and sooner, than he did with the Los Angeles Kings. And that's such a double-edged sword.

One of the biggest concerns about Clarke at the time was his skating technique. But there was just as much praise for his consistent activation and deception, which suggested he could anchor a power play for years to come.

We're starting to see that potential with the Kings. The question is whether Clarke would have developed the same way in Arizona and later Utah, or whether his skating would have been a greater obstacle in a different development environment.

Even if that path might not have been ideal for Clarke, he would have been an excellent addition to Arizona's blue line.

10. Ottawa Senators: Logan Stankoven, Center

Current Carolina Hurricane and recent Stanley Cup champion Logan Stankoven, originally a Dallas Stars draft pick, seemed to be overlooked for size reasons.

Thankfully, we have the benefit of hindsight to confirm that his size did not end up being a problem.

When looking at this draft, Stankoven could have gone anywhere from here at 10th overall to about 15th, but when taking team need into account, the original pick, Tyler Boucher, has only played two NHL games.

The Senators reached for Boucher at No. 10, so the question here goes beyond whether they should have selected him. It's which alternative would have been the best choice.

We briefly considered Kent Johnson, along with Cole Sillinger and Matthew Coronato. There's a case for each, but Stankoven ultimately gets the nod for two reasons: his relentless motor and his ability to influence play shift after shift.

He moves the puck quickly rather than holding it too long, and he attacks the interior instead of settling for the perimeter.

That combination would make him a valuable addition to Ottawa's lineup.

articles.title: Week 12 Waiver Wire Fantasy Projections for Top Pickups and Sleeper Targets
articles.summary: The NFL season has pushed past this year's "bye-pocalypse" and will feature a full 16-game slate for Thanksgiving Week. However, this doesn't mean that fantasy football managers won't need to play the waiver wire in Week 12.
articles.body:
The NFL season has pushed past this year's "bye-pocalypse" and will feature a full 16-game slate for Thanksgiving Week. However, this doesn't mean that fantasy football managers won't need to play the waiver wire in Week 12.

Injuries are still a significant factor. Brock Bowers and Jordan Addison were among the players who missed Week 11, while Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was placed in the concussion protocol following his game.

Here, we'll examine some top waiver-wire targets for Week 12, examine their individual matchups, and make a few predictions.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

As one might expect, New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith had miserable fantasy outings against the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills in Weeks 9 and 10. However, he got to face a suspect defense in Week 11 and delivered.

Smith threw three touchdown passes and amassed 19.4 fantasy points against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.

This week, Smith will face another middling defense when the Jets visit the Miami Dolphins. While Miami won the first meeting of the season, Smith finished that game with 24.5 fantasy points.

Smith is only rostered in 19 percent of fantasy leagues.

Week 12 Projection: 256 yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT

The Cleveland Browns have a bad offensive line and have struggled to run the ball effectively all season. They've regularly relied on screens and short passes to help augment the ground game, a process made easier by the Week 7 return of Dylan Sampson.

Quinshon Judkins is still Cleveland's starter, but Sampson has served as the primary receiving back, when healthy, since early in his 2025 rookie campaign. He's caught 16 of 22 targets in four games since his return, and he's reached double-digit fantasy points twice over that span.

Sampson hasn't fallen below seven fantasy points in a game this season and has a favorable matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Las Vegas has surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing RBs. Sampson is rostered in only 24 percent of fantasy leagues.

Week 12 Projection: 5 receptions, 59 scrimmage yards

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

Following his breakthrough performance in Monday's upset win over the Cincinnati Bengals, Antonio Williams is likely to be the top waiver target of Week 12. He should be.

The Washington Commanders rookie has pushed himself into a prominent role, and he shined brightly under the Monday night spotlight. He caught nine of 11 targets for 122 yards, and he finished with 21.2 fantasy points.

Williams also caught both of Jayden Daniels' passes on the final game-winning drive and will undoubtedly have his quarterback's trust moving forward as a result.

This week, the Commanders will visit the Arizona Cardinals, who have surrendered the 10th-most fantasy points to opposing WRs. Williams is currently rostered in just 31 percent of leagues.

Week 12 Projection: 6 receptions, 76 yards

Williams wasn't the only waiver target who made a statement on Monday night. Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki showed that if a defense can take away top receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, Cincinnati's passing attack will still function.

Washington held Chase and Higgins to just 74 combined receiving yards, though Higgins did find the end zone. With those two drawing so much defensive attention, Gesicki went off for five catches and 77 yards.

Gesicki's production has been erratic this season, and he wasn't heavily targeted in blowout wins over the Atlanta Falcons and Pittsburgh Steelers. However, he's topped 10 fantasy points five times and could approach that mark against the New Orleans Saints.

The Saints have surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends. Gesicki is rostered in only 45 percent of fantasy leagues.

Week 12 Projection: 4 receptions, 42 yards, 1 TD

*Fantasy roster and scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Week 12 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice for Fringe Flex Fantasy Football Starters
articles.summary: Week 12 will feature several intriguing matchups spread across multiple days. The week's action will begin with Wednesday's game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
Week 12 will feature several intriguing matchups spread across multiple days. The week's action will begin with Wednesday's game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams.

Don't forget to have lineups set and waiver claims in early this week.

While all 32 teams will be in action, some managers will still find themselves leaning on fringe starters because of injuries. Here, you'll find early start/sit advice for some of the best and worst matchups in point-per-reception (PPR) play.

Start: Samaje Perine, Cincinnati Bengals

Cincinnati Bengals backup Samaje Perine is a sleeper candidate who is still available in over 70 percent of fantasy leagues. He's also worth considering in the flex this season.

Perine has often been a more effective runner than starter Chase Brown this season, and he's regularly on the field on receiving downs. He caught four passes on Monday and finished with 13.7 fantasy points.

Don't be surprised if Perine gets a steady workload as the Bengals look to get back on track in Week 12. Cincinnati doesn't like to run the ball, but the New Orleans Saints have surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing RBs.

Fantasy managers rejoiced when Kyle Monangai made his return from a thumb injury in Week 11. Many of them quickly turned to cursing the Chicago Bears for not giving him more opportunities.

D'Andre Swift held a heavy workload against the New Orleans Saints, while Monangai finished with just eight carries and 1.8 fantasy points.

This week, the Bears will face a Detroit Lions defense that has surrendered the fifth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs. Monangai should eventually return to fantasy form, but don't bet on it happening this week.

Start: Jakobi Meyers, Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jacksonville Jaguars stumbled against the New York Giants in Week 11, losing for the first time since Week 6. Trevor Lawrence struggled mightily against a ferocious New York pass rush, but Jakobi Meyers managed to shine as an outlet option.

Meyers caught just four passes but tallied 85 yards.

This week, the Jags will look to rebound against the rival Tennessee Titans, and Meyers could have an even bigger day. Laim Coen isn't afraid of running up the score, and the Titans have surrendered the most fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf got himself ejected from Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. While Metcalf avoided suspension , it's impossible to trust him this week in a critical Black Friday matchup.

Metcalf has reached double-digit fantasy points only once in his last four games, and he's likely to draw regular matchups with star Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II on Friday.

As a team, the Broncos have surrendered the fifth-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers. Add in the overall struggles of their passing game recently, and Metcalf is a player to avoid.

The Washington Commanders were able to corral the Bengals' offense, largely by limiting top receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Of course, that opened things up nicely for tight end and de facto third receiver Mike Gesicki.

Gesicki finished Monday's game with five catches and 12.7 fantasy points.

The Saints are likely to take a similar defensive approach this week, and they have surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends. For managers who need help at the position, Gesicki is still available in over 50 percent of leagues.

Baltimore Ravens tight end Mark Andrews found some fantasy life in his first game with bridge quarterback Jacoby Brissett. However, he was back to being a bit of an afterthought in Week 11.

Though the Ravens passed often during their 35-33 loss, Andrews caught just two of three targets for 14 yards.

This week, Baltimore will face a Houston Texans defense that hasn't been great but has stifled opposing tight ends. No team has surrendered fewer fantasy points to the position this season.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: 1 Thing Every NFL Fanbase Should Actually Be Thankful For Right Now
articles.summary: Thanksgiving has arrived, with nearly a third of the NFL's 32 teams in action between Wednesday and Friday.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving has arrived, with nearly a third of the NFL's 32 teams in action between Wednesday and Friday.

Nobody is close to perfect, and some teams have already seen their Super Bowl hopes fade to a long shot this season. But everybody has at least something to be thankful for this time of year.

Here is one reason for every fanbase to feel good as we embark on the holiday season, which coincides with the home stretch of the NFL campaign.

The winningest franchise in the NFL this decade has fallen short of the Super Bowl every year in the Josh Allen era, but they've never been a No. 1 seed. After major offseason changes, they're all alone atop the AFC following a 9-1 start. Allen remains the centerpiece, but Joe Brady is in charge now, and fresh names like Jim Leonhard, DJ Moore and Amani Hooker are making a major impact.

Miami Dolphins: The players appear to be fully behind this regime

This team lacks talent and experience and is currently missing its franchise quarterback, but it's clear the players fight hard for Jeff Hafley. Miami is 1-4 in one-score games, and despite mounting injuries, the defense has been decent most of the season.

New England Patriots: Drake Maye has proved 2025 wasn't an aberration

After coming painfully close to winning MVP last season, Maye got off to a rocky start before carrying the team with 14 touchdown passes to two interceptions and a 122.2 passer rating over a five-week hot streak. We might not see him again this year, but at least the Pats can be pretty sure he's the guy moving forward.

New York Jets: David Bailey is already becoming a star

It'll be another losing season for a team that may face significant offseason changes, but Bailey has been absolutely phenomenal as a rookie No. 2 overall pick. He leads the NFL with six forced fumbles (five of which have come in the last five games) and ranks third with 9.5 sacks, but his impact goes beyond the numbers. The 23-year-old already looks like a game-wrecker.

Baltimore Ravens: Mike Green has emerged

The sophomore second-round pick shined the last two weeks against the Chargers and Panthers, registering four sacks to bring his season total to 7.5. At 23 years old, Green looks like a legitimate pass-rushing piece to build around moving forward.

Cincinnati Bengals: Joe Burrow remains healthy behind a highly reliable offensive line

The prime MVP candidate remains on track to start all 17 games for just the second time in his career, thanks in large part to an offensive line that Pro Football Focus ranks fifth in pass-blocking efficiency. He's one of only nine qualified quarterbacks who have been sacked on fewer than five percent of their dropbacks, and that's got Cincinnati in the Super Bowl hunt.

Cleveland Browns: The rebuild is way ahead of schedule

These guys traded away their best player in his prime, and yet here they are, on track to record just their fourth double-digit-win campaign this century. The offense has a long way to go, but there are a lot of enticing pieces in place for a team that is headed in the right direction.

Pittsburgh Steelers: The return of Michael Pittman Jr. from a foot injury

Can the two-time 1,000-yard receiver stop the bleeding for an offense that has generated three total touchdowns in back-to-back crushing losses? Who knows, but at least the Steelers will have a new element in the equation against the Broncos on Friday.

Houston Texans: C.J. Stroud might be the guy after all

The 4-6 Texans remain a long shot for the playoffs, but that surprisingly has nothing to do with Stroud. The rookie phenom from 2023 who became a liability in 2024 and 2025 has exploded just in the nick of time with the best season of his career. Barely 25 years old, Stroud is the league's sixth-highest-rated qualified passer with 22 touchdowns to four interceptions.

Indianapolis Colts: Carlie Irsay-Gordon is not messing around

Relatively new in the role of CEO, Irsay-Gordon has taken a cutthroat approach to a team that appeared to be slipping into football purgatory early this season. She proactively sold off expensive and aging parts at the trade deadline and shockingly cut Daniel Jones last week. It's clear she will not settle for mediocrity long term.

Jacksonville Jaguars: Trevor Lawrence has finally become elite

Lawrence struggled in a Week 11 loss to the Giants, but that was an outlier in what has been a superb second season in Liam Coen's offense. In his last 17 starts (the equivalent of one full regular season), the 27-year-old former top pick has gone 14-3 with 40 touchdown passes, 11 interceptions and a 106.6 passer rating.

Tennessee Titans: Cam Ward is playing the best football of his career

The top pick of the 2025 draft has been a disappointment in general for a team still stuck deep in a rebuild, but the under-supported 24-year-old has really kicked it up a notch with six touchdown passes to one interception and a 103.9 rating over the last three weeks. Now we'll see if he can sustain this to give the team added confidence entering Year 3 of the Ward era.

Denver Broncos: The rise of Jonah Coleman

The Broncos found themselves in the throes of a running back problem early on, but the rookie fourth-round pick has come to the rescue with 390 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns over his last four games—all of which were wins. He's emerged as the favorite to win Offensive Rookie of the Year .

Kansas City Chiefs: The schedule thus far

Per ESPN's Football Power Index , the Chiefs have feasted on the easiest schedule in the NFL to date, with comfortable wins over the Dolphins, Chargers, Jets, Falcons and Cardinals keeping them in contention for the AFC West crown. But their next three road games are against the Bills, Rams and Bengals, and they have the 49ers a couple of weeks after that. The good news is they've at least built up a playoff cushion in the first 11 weeks.

Las Vegas Raiders: The remaining schedule

Meanwhile, per the same source, the Raiders have the league's easiest remaining schedule. If they can take care of the Browns this week, they'll be in the driver's seat for a late surge with the Chargers, Titans and Cardinals still on their slate following a Week 13 bye.

Los Angeles Chargers: Akheem Mesidor is on the right track

Finding a silver lining with this 1-9 Chargers team ain't easy, but at least their 2026 first-round pick looks like a hit. Mesidor is the highest-graded qualified player on the entire roster at Pro Football Focus .

Dallas Cowboys: They are so entertaining

It sure doesn't look as though the defensively inept Cowboys are about to bust out of that three-decade Super Bowl drought, but Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb are a show, and Dallas has the NFL's third-ranked scoring offense. In their last two games alone, 167 points have been scored.

It's hard to believe this team is ready for a real run, especially considering the quarterback situation with Jaxson Dart down. That said, the defense has proven to be a force, and Dart and/or J.J. McCarthy appear to have a strong supporting cast on both sides of the ball.

Philadelphia Eagles: They've been to 3 of the last 9 Super Bowls

When you're playing out a lost season at 3-7 and you're a veteran team like the Eagles, you can't really take solace in much. A rebuild may be on the horizon, which is why Eagles fans have to remind themselves that they've had one hell of a successful decade to hang their hats on.

Washington Commanders: There's a path to the division title

All seemed hopeless when poor game management potentially cost them two wins in October, but this squad deserves plenty of credit for a 3-1 post-bye run to remain within two games of the division-leading Giants. Keep in mind that the remaining schedule is soft and that they already hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over New York.

Chicago Bears: Ryan Poles isn't satisfied

The Bears were already a prime Super Bowl contender as the trade deadline approached, but then the general manager went out and acquired Jeffery Simmons to bolster the defense in preparation for a very feasible run at their first Lombardi Trophy in four decades. Those types of moves win titles.

Detroit Lions: They can outscore their defensive problems

It'll be super tough sledding in this division without Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell on defense, but the Lions always have a shot with Jared Goff handing the ball to Jahmyr Gibbs, throwing to Amon-Ra St. Brown and receiving protection from arguably the best offensive line in the league.

Green Bay Packers: The return of Micah Parsons

It's wild to think that this defense has already shined on plenty of occasions despite not having its superstar pass rusher. With Parsons set to make his season debut, the sky really is the limit for a D that ranks second in the NFL with 20 takeaways.

Arguably the best coordinator in the sport, Flores has the Vikings in contention despite an offense that ranks 28th in scoring and 29th in EPA per play. Now that they've survived the first half of the season thanks to Flores' unit and brought back Kirk Cousins, the Vikings remain in the picture atop the mighty NFC North.

Atlanta Falcons: They're in the NFC South

In terms of net EPA per play, this is the seventh-worst team in the NFL. They've been outscored 85-30 over the course of three consecutive losses, and it's still unclear if they have their franchise quarterback. It'd be bleak if not for the fact they remain just two games back in this punch line of a division.

Carolina leads said punch line by two games, thanks primarily to the fact only two defenses have forced more takeaways. The Panthers forced six turnovers while beating the Saints and Ravens by a combined five points over the last two weeks. And while Devin Lloyd stands out, it's generally been a team effort. Kudos to Todd Wash for the job he's done since taking over for the fired Ejiro Evero.

New Orleans Saints: Four more divisional games

A team that is just 2-6 since nearly beating the Lions and then defeating the Ravens in the first two weeks is in big trouble. That said, at least New Orleans still plays the Buccaneers twice and the Falcons and Panthers once each between now and Week 18. The Saints have plenty of control over their path.

The Bucs have an NFL-high 21 takeaways entering Week 12, 11 of which have come in their three wins. Thank goodness for a defense that somewhat quietly ranks near the top of the league in EPA per play.

Arizona Cardinals: Jeremiyah Love should be back soon?

The question mark is there for a reason. The rookie third overall pick struggled to make a significant impact before a high-ankle sprain landed him on IR at the start of this month. Still, his pending return will give fans of a sorry team something to watch with an eye toward the future.

Los Angeles Rams: Their pre-bye week schedule

The preseason Super Bowl favorites merely survived the first half of the season. It helped that, just when the receiving corps was being gutted by injuries, they were lucky enough to draw the Raiders, Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals. Four wins during that pre-bye stretch have them very much alive at 6-4, but the schedule becomes brutal now. We'll see if they can continue treading water while awaiting the return of Davante Adams and holding out hope for a playoff comeback from Puka Nacua.

San Francisco 49ers: This just might be the year

Have the injury gods been kinder? Only a little. The 49ers have still been hit hard in that department, but an onslaught of injuries in 2024 and 2025 seems to have made them that much more resilient. Now, even far from 100 percent, they're wrecking teams while emerging as the clear-cut Super Bowl favorite. Is it finally going to happen for Kyle Shanahan and Co.?

Sam Darnold hasn't been healthy or particularly productive, but Lock has stepped in and won all three of his starts while posting a ridiculous 125.6 passer rating over four appearances (all victories). It has to be good to know that even if Darnold turns out to be somewhat of a one-hit wonder in Seattle, the team might actually have another viable option in Lock.
