articles.title: New Cowboys Rumors as NFL Insiders Sound Off on Brian Schottenheimer's Hot Seat As HC
articles.summary: Having already taken play-calling duties away from defensive coordinator Christian Parker, much of the focus for the Dallas Cowboys now is on Brian Schottenheimer if he can do enough down the stretch to retain his job as head coach after this season.
articles.body:
Having already taken play-calling duties away from defensive coordinator Christian Parker, much of the focus for the Dallas Cowboys now is on Brian Schottenheimer if he can do enough down the stretch to retain his job as head coach after this season.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano , Schottenheimer might be in a position where he needs to lead the Cowboys to the playoffs to "ensure" Jerry Jones brings him back in 2027.

Graziano noted there could be "some smoke" around Schottenheimer if the Cowboys miss the playoffs and the hiring of Parker, who is a first-time defensive coordinator, ends up not working out.

Clark Addresses Pettine-Parker Relationship

Amid the ongoing defensive struggles this season, the Cowboys announced last week that Parker would no longer call plays on that side of the ball. Mike Pettine, who joined the defensive staff in mid-October, took over as play-caller.

Fowler noted the decision to take some of Parker's responsibilities away was "not universally well-received" within the Cowboys facilities. Parker didn't hide that he was unhappy about the situation.

If there is a feather in Scottenheimer's cap, even without a playoff appearance, it's that his background is as an offensive coach and the Cowboys have been aces on that side of the ball.

Dallas currently ranks third in the NFL in points per game after putting up 91 points in the last two weeks and at least 27 points in five consecutive games.

It also helps that Jones has historically given head coaches a long window. The last Cowboys head coach who didn't coach into their fourth season was Dave Campo, who was fired after his third year in 2002.

Wade Phillips was fired midway through his fourth season after a 1-7 start in 2010.

Scottenheimer is currently in his second season as Cowboys head coach. He is 12-15-1 overall, including a 6-3 mark against NFC East opponents.

Dallas has a quick turnaround this week as it prepares to host the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day at 4:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: New Puka Nacua Rumors on WR's Rams Future, Potential Franchise Tag After Knee Injury
articles.summary: With Puka Nacua potentially out for the season, his long-term outlook as a member of the Los Angeles Rams is more uncertain than ever.
articles.body:
With Puka Nacua potentially out for the season, his long-term outlook as a member of the Los Angeles Rams is more uncertain than ever.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano , Nacua is more likely to get the franchise tag this offseason than a multiyear contract from the Rams because of his injury situation and off-field issues.

Fowler cited multiple NFL scouts and executives who believe the Rams' "best course" of action with Nacua in the offseason is to use the franchise tag.

Graziano added it's not "out of the question" the Rams would do a long-term deal, but they "didn't seem to even do much work toward a possible extension" last offseason.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , people in the league "find it hard to believe" Nacua will get to unrestricted free agency and the non-exclusive franchise tag could help the Rams in multiple ways.

The tag gives the Rams more time to negotiate a long-term deal, but they could also receive two first-round picks back if a team were to sign Nacua to an offer sheet they didn't want to match.

It's extremely rare a player on the non-franchise tag gets an offer sheet because of the draft compensation attached. The last time it happened was in 2000 when Joey Galloway left the Seattle Seahawks to sign with the Dallas Cowboys.

The projected tag number for wide receivers in 2027 is $30.9 million, which would only be the 12th-highest salary for the position next season based on current contracts.

One potential stumbling block for the Rams is the tag is fully guaranteed. They are currently projected to have $80.6 million in cap space next season, but Nacua, Kobie Turner and Byron Young are all set to hit free agency.

Nacua is likely done for the season after undergoing surgery to repair an MCL injury. He was also recently suspended three games by the NFL for violating the personal conduct policy. The league is allowing him to serve the suspension while injured.

If Nacua doesn't play again in 2026, he will finish the season with 715 receiving yards and four touchdowns in seven games. It will be the second time in the last three seasons he has missed at least six games.

Since entering the NFL in 2023, Nacua ranks in the top five among all receivers in receptions and receiving yards.

articles.title: NFL Thanksgiving preview: Bears and Lions bring two fun offenses to battle for first place in NFC North
articles.summary: The Lions and Bears are both 8-2 heading into a huge Thanksgiving game.
articles.body:
Ben Johnson is a fantastic offensive play-caller, as he is showing as head coach of the Chicago Bears.

But even though Johnson left the Detroit Lions as their offensive coordinator almost two years ago, their offense has been just fine as well.

We could see one of the higher scoring games of the NFL season on Thursday when the Lions and Bears meet up. Both offenses are in the NFL's top eight in yards gained and points scored. That's a big reason Chicago and Detroit are tied atop the NFC North at 8-2.

Johnson has transformed the Bears franchise since becoming their head coach in 2025. The Bears are eighth in yardage and points this season, and that's with Caleb Williams missing three games due to a hamstring injury. Chicago is good in the run game, with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai both capable of big games, and they have weapons like Luther Burden III, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland in an explosive passing game. The defense has also been very good since trading for Jeffery Simmons, who had three sacks in a win over the Saints last week.

For the Lions, it's mostly the same stars from when Johnson was their offensive coordinator. Jared Goff is an efficient quarterback with 20 touchdowns and just four interceptions this season; Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Wiliams and Sam LaPorta are an excellent pass-catching trio; and running back Jahmyr Gibbs is on a historic pace. He has 1,502 yards from scrimmage and 15 touchdowns in 10 games.

"If he's not the offensive player of the year right now, then he's got to be top three because he's all over the place," Johnson said, via A to Z Sports . "He's leading the league in scrimmage yards — run game, pass game. It just seems like they can't get the ball to him enough so we've got our hands full with him."

The winner will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North. It will take a lot of points to get the win.

The Lions probably need it a little more simply because they're at home. The Bears get the return match at Chicago in Week 17. However, Chicago has the third-toughest remaining schedule in the NFL via DVOA , so the argument can be made that the Bears can't afford the loss. The winner will have a one-game lead and the first step toward clinching the tiebreaker. Even if the Lions need it more, it's not by much.

Simmons could end up being one of the greatest in-season trade additions of all time. The Bears traded two first-round picks to the Titans for Simmons, a first-team All-Pro last season, and he has been dominant. He has five sacks in three games. The Bears haven't trailed since Simmons came aboard; their streak of not trailing for five straight games is the longest for the franchise since 1985. Simmons' presence has been huge for defensive end Montez Sweat, who has a sack in two of the three games Simmons has been alongside him. The Lions have allowed 22 sacks this season. How they're able to control Simmons in the middle could determine who wins on Thursday.

The 8-2 Lions host the 8-2 Bears in a game in which both teams have over a 90% chance to make the postseason, per ESPN's FPI. This game was Lions -2.5 in the offseason, but has re-opened Lions +2.5 — Chicago adding Jeffrey Simmons, while Detroit has lost both Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson for the season has a lot to do with that movement. This will likely only be the second time all season that the Lions have been an underdog (+5.5 at Buffalo in a 41-31 loss in Week 2). Detroit's defense has been improving after a horrific start to the season, allowing 21 points or fewer during its six-game winning streak — and now it has Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch again in the back end. With the week's highest total (55.5), expect fireworks on offense. However, I think this one is a little lower-scoring than the market anticipates. Detroit is only 3-2 to the over at home. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

The NFL North lead is on the line when the Bears take on the Lions, and the total is set at a juicy 55.5 points. Here are three themes to track from a fantasy perspective.

1. How much volume will the Chicago passing game get? We had big dreams for Caleb Williams and friends when the season started, excited about the passing elements and suspecting that the Chicago defense would be poor, forcing weekly shootouts. Alas, the Bears have been better on defense than expected, and Williams has yet to throw more than 37 passes in any game. There has still been production, but it's been partially muted. Detroit's secondary has been gettable all year.

2. Who will be the odd man out in the Detroit offense? We expect Jahmyr Gibbs to come home in every fantasy start, but usually there's one underperforming player between Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Sam LaPorta — there's only one football to go around. LaPorta hasn't scored a touchdown in five weeks, though he's still a possible starter for fantasy managers given how thin tight end has played this year.

3. Is Kyle Monangai ready for a bigger role? Monangai had a couple of monster games in the first month of the year, but his return last week from toe and thumb injuries was a disappointment (8-18-0 rushing, no receptions). D'Andre Swift has been reliable all year, but Ben Johnson would prefer a two-headed backfield if all parties are hale. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: Courtland Sutton's Cryptic IG Photos Go Viral After Broncos' Win vs. Raiders
articles.summary: After failing to record a catch in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Denver Broncos veteran wide receiver Courtland Sutton caused a bit of a stir on social media.
articles.body:
After failing to record a catch in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Denver Broncos veteran wide receiver Courtland Sutton caused a bit of a stir on social media.

Sutton took to Instagram to post two pictures of his "highlights" from Sunday's win, which went viral because they both featured him blocking Raiders defensive backs to open up the Broncos' run game:

While some may have viewed Sutton's posts as trolling, others didn't see it that way. Chris Raff of 93.7 The Ticket noted that Sutton has a reputation for his "leadership, downfield blocking and loyalty" to Denver.

Sutton was targeted just twice in Sunday's game and failed to complete a catch both times. Through 10 games this season, he's recorded 25 catches for 266 yards and two touchdowns, reaching the 50-yard mark in just one game. His massive drop-off is a surprise after he posted back-to-back 1,000-yard campaigns in 2024 and 2025.

Despite Sutton's struggles, the Broncos haven't skipped a beat, ranking second in the AFC with an 8-2 record. As one of the top contenders in the conference, Denver should feel confident that it can still find success when one of its top players underperforms.

Sutton and the Broncos will look to extend their win streak to seven straight games when they meet the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) on Black Friday.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Patriots' View of A.J. Brown's Struggles in 1st Season After Trade From Eagles
articles.summary: A.J. Brown's injury issues in his first season with the New England Patriots have raised "massive questions" about three full seasons remaining on his contract, The Athletic's Chad Graff reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
A.J. Brown's injury issues in his first season with the New England Patriots have raised "massive questions" about three full seasons remaining on his contract, The Athletic's Chad Graff reported Wednesday.

Brown, who has recorded just 11 catches and 128 receiving yards in four games this season, is signed through 2029 but has no guaranteed money past 2027.

"Here's the way Patriots sources put Brown's struggles: A strong training camp had him in line for a good season, but then a high ankle sprain lingered and continued to slow him even when he returned," Graff reported. "Then, a knee injury further limited him, hurting his chemistry with Maye and throwing off his timing and route running. And now, the hamstring injury has hampered him even further."

Graff concluded, "It's effectively a lost season for Brown, and there are massive questions going into next year when he will be a 30-year-old wide receiver entering his final season with guaranteed money in his contract."

The Patriots acquired Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in June in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-rounder.

The move came a year after Brown had signed a three-year, $96 million extension through 2028. Spotrac reported at the time of the trade, however, that Brown had just $33 million remaining in guaranteed money ($29 million for 2026, $4 million for 2027) on the deal.

Brown first hit injured reserve after suffering an ankle injury in Week 1. He returned for Weeks 6 and 7 before he was sidelined for another two games due to knee issues .

Head coach Mike Vrabel later denied reports that he and the Tennessee Titans had known Brown had knee issues before trading him in 2022.

The wide receiver returned to the lineup in Week 10 only to suffer a hamstring injury ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss reported is expected to sideline him for "multiple weeks."

Those injuries aren't the only concern for Brown, who has also struggled with drops when available to join the lineup.

Brown has $4 million in 2027 guarantees set to kick in on the third day of the league year, per Spotrac . Whether the Patriots feel Brown can bounce back from his production struggles if he can stay healthy next season could impact whether the team considers taking an out on the contract that would leave the franchise with $25.7 million in dead cap, according to Spotrac.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Hints at Potential Decision on NFL Future After 100th Game in Chiefs' Arrowhead Stadium
articles.summary: After playing his 100th game at Arrowhead Stadium this past Sunday, Kansas City Chiefs star tight end Travis Kelce doesn't appear to be slowing down anytime soon.
articles.body:
After playing his 100th game at Arrowhead Stadium this past Sunday, Kansas City Chiefs star tight end Travis Kelce doesn't appear to be slowing down anytime soon.

After recording six catches for 74 yards and two touchdowns in a 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals, Kelce boldly declared, "Cheers to 100 more!" However, his brother, Jason, questioned whether he really planned to hit another century mark, and the 37-year-old admitted he may not get that far.

"Yeah, you're right, I won't," Kelce said on this week's episode of the New Heights podcast. "But cheers to 100 more. Who knows how many I'll get to?"

Still, it sounds like Kelce has left the door open on potentially returning for a 15th NFL season. When Jason pushed further and asked if he was confirming his return for the 2027 campaign, the 11-time Pro Bowler remained coy.

"No, I'm not confirming it," Kelce said. "I'm not confirming it, but..."

Kelce will try to continue to turn back the clock when the Chiefs (8-2) face the Buffalo Bills (9-1) on Thanksgiving Night.

articles.title: How Much Money Aaron Rodgers Has Left on His Steelers Contract amid Release Rumors
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers made the surprise decision to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers with more than a third of his guaranteed contract remaining.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers made the surprise decision to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers with more than a third of his guaranteed contract remaining.

Rodgers has $8.5 million left of his fully guaranteed $22 million deal, according to Spotrac.

He will also be owed $625,000 per playoff win if he plays in 75 percent of the Steelers' regular-season snaps, according to Spotrac.

Rodgers had played 97 percent of the team's offensive snaps so far this season, per Pro Football Reference , before the Steelers announced he would be inactive for Friday's matchup against the Denver Broncos.

The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette 's Gerry Dulac reported "the Steelers spent Monday and Tuesday preparing for the Broncos as though Rodgers would be the starter" before "something happened Tuesday evening" that led to the team naming Mason Rudolph Friday's starter.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Wednesday morning Rodgers had not been spotted at the Steelers facility, and "it seems like a release is destined to happen."

ESPN's Adam Schefter added later in the day Rodgers had been "excused from being at the team facility today while he processes his benching." NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported as of Wednesday morning "there is no indication right now that the Steelers intend to release" Rodgers.

Rodgers joined the Steelers in May on a one-year deal worth up to $25 million ahead of what he said would be his final NFL season.

He led the Steelers to a 6-4 start while completing 60.9 percent of his passes for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdowns and six interceptions.

Rodgers had averaged a career-low 6.2 yards per pass attempt over that span, per ESPN Insights .

He was also coming off a loss at the Philadelphia Eagles during which he took five sacks for 45 yards despite being pressured on 13 percent of his dropbacks, per initial Pro Football Focus stats cited by NFL reporter Jon Ledyard .

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Wednesday the relationship between Rodgers and Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy "has not been in a good place."

"The frustration is not just with Rodgers," Schultz reported. "Multiple position groups have been upset, and I'm told McCarthy has not been what some offensive players hoped for. Frustration has been growing among everyone for weeks."

Rudolph has three days to respond to his surprise promotion to QB1 before the Steelers kick off Friday afternoon against the visiting Broncos. The Steelers (6-4) currently trail the Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) and Cleveland Browns (6-4) for the AFC North lead, and their playoff odds could drop to 55 percent with a loss or climb to 76 percent with a win, per NFL Next Gen Stats .

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III's Status for Chiefs vs. Bills Revealed amid Groin Injury Rehab
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will be facing the 9-1 Buffalo Bills without their star running back.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs will be facing the 9-1 Buffalo Bills without their star running back.

Kenneth Walker III will sit out his third straight game this Thursday when the Chiefs play on Thanksgiving in Buffalo, the team announced Wednesday.

Walker has been sidelined for the Chiefs' last two games with a groin injury. He rejoined practice Tuesday for the first time since suffering his injury but was listed as "limited."

Walker has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 groin injury that requires "two to three weeks rest," per NFL Network and ESPN's Jeffri Chadiha .

It has been 13 days since Walker suffered his injury during a Nov. 12 practice.

Chadiha noted Walker's return might have been impacted by the Chiefs' quick turnaround between last Sunday's win over the Arizona Cardinals and Thursday's holiday matchup. The Thursday game could also be impacted by rain.

Rookie running back Emmett Johnson is set to start Thursday in Walker's place, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Johnson, who has started in relief of Walker for the past two weeks, has recorded 206 rushing yards and a touchdown over that span.

The Bills have tied for the best 10-game start in franchise history thanks in large part to running one of the NFL's highest-scoring offenses. The team has allowed the eight-fewest rushing yards against (94.1 per game) so far this season.

Buffalo is also coming off the first three-game stretch without a touchdown allowed over a 43-drive scoreless stretch that marks the NFL's longest since 2019, although that run took place against three injury-limited opponents in the Minnesota Vikings, New York Jets and Miami Dolphins.

Johnson could continue making his case for a bigger role in the Chiefs' lineup if he is able to help his team snap that streak Thursday.

After the Bills, the Chiefs are slated face the most effective run defense in the league in a Dec. 3 Thursday matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk Agrees to Commanders Contract, Latest Details on WR After 49ers Release
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders will sign free agent wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk to a practice squad contract.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders will sign free agent wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk to a practice squad contract.

Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk's agent, confirmed the news to ESPN's Adam Schefter on Wednesday, shortly after the wide receiver was in for a visit.

Aiyuk, who last played in 2024, was released Monday by the San Francisco 49ers.

Front Office Sports' Mark Maske reported Aiyuk's "signing won't be officially completed today."

The report comes after Commanders general manager Adam Peters said in a Wednesday morning appearance on 106.7 The Fan his team had "genuine interest" in Aiyuk.

Peters praised Aiyuk has a "smart player" whose "work ethic" he had seen demonstrated during their time overlapping with the San Francisco 49ers, but also noted he hasn't seen NFL action in more than two years.

"You can work as hard as you want, but there's a difference between being in shape and being in football shape... Those are the things we'll have to look at, and see where he's at," Peters said. "I think we'd all be foolish to say that he's going to jump right on to where he left off."

Aiyuk suffered a severe knee injury in October 2024 that sidelined him for the rest of that season, then split from the 49ers in 2025 amid a reported dispute over the team's involvement in his rehabilitation.

The wide receiver repeatedly expressed interest in playing for the Commanders in social media posts ahead of the 2026 season, although there were reportedly concerns over his social media presence and his relationship with former ASU teammate Jayden Daniels.

The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala recently reported Aiyuk and Daniels "are now on good terms."

After struggling early this season as Daniels dealt with injury issues, Washington has gone 3-1 since the team's Week 7 bye. The Commanders (4-5-1) remain two games of the New York Giants (6-3-1) and Dallas Cowboys (5-6) for the NFC East lead.

Whether Peters feels Aiyuk is in good enough shape to help Daniels and his team chase the division title could determine if the wide receiver is ultimately elevated to the active roster down the stretch of the season.

articles.summary: Aiyuk is looking to play in his first NFL game since 2024.
articles.body:
Veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad as a free agent, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.

Aiyuk was released by the 49ers on Monday and passed through waivers on Tuesday, going unclaimed. Now, he reunites with his former teammate at Arizona State, quarterback Jayden Daniels.

The Commanders, fresh off a stunning upset over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 11, have been in need of help at receiver following a season-ending injury to star wideout Terry McLaurin. The team sits at 4-5-1, just two games back from the New York Giants, who hold the lead in the NFC East.

This marks a fresh start for the 28-year-old, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers ahead of the 2024 season but played just seven games on the new deal. He tore his ACL and MCL on Oct. 20, 2024, ending his season.

Aiyuk also missed the entirety of the 2025 season, with conflicting reports about his health as he rehabbed the knee injury. The distance between the two sides only grew as San Francisco voided his contract guarantees ahead of the 2025 season. Eventually, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December 2025 due to his continued absence and lack of communication with the team.

This past January, 49ers GM John Lynch officially acknowledged the impending split, saying at his end-of-season news conference, "I think it's safe to say he's played his last snap with the 49ers."

Aiyuk was officially reinstated from the Reserve/Left Squad list on Nov. 9, at which time the 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption to decide if they wanted to release him, trade him or add him to the 53-man roster. The reinstatement was the first step toward Aiyuk's eventual release.

San Francisco drafted him with the 25th pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. He had his breakout season in 2022, finishing with 1,015 yards and eight touchdowns. Aiyuk returned in 2023 and improved, finishing with 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.

articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce told reporters on Wednesday that he suffered a partially torn Achilles during his team's 33-30 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce told reporters on Wednesday that he suffered a partially torn Achilles during his team's 33-30 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2.

Pierce had heel and ankle surgery in March in response to issues he was having. He is still hoping to return sometime this season.

Pierce had led the NFL in yards per catch each of the past two seasons (22.3 in 2024 and 21.3 in 2025).

Last year, Pierce amassed a career-high 1,003 receiving yards on just 47 catches. He re-signed with the Colts on a four-year, $114 million contract in free agency.

"It definitely got a little bit worse as the (2025) season went," Pierce said of his ankle issues in June. "Probably the last month I'd say I was kind of struggling – (it) affected practice, I'd taken some days off. I'm glad they figured out what the issue was and we were able to fix it."

Pierce got a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection shortly after the 2025 season ended. However, the injection and ensuing rehab didn't work, and he underwent a clean-up procedure (ankle surgery) in the spring.

Hopefully Pierce is able to return soon enough, although he is running out of time to get back this season with the Colts having just six games remaining.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Rips Mike McCarthy, Reveals Behind-the-Scenes Issues Before Steelers Benching
articles.summary: After surprisingly being benched for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers didn't hold back on head coach Mike McCarthy.
articles.body:
After surprisingly being benched for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers didn't hold back on head coach Mike McCarthy.

Rodgers made a surprise appearance on Wednesday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show and revealed that he hasn't spoken to McCarthy since before his benching was announced, and he was informed of the team's decision while he was on a phone call with tight end Pat Freiermuth.

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

James Harrison Backs Up Rodgers' Stories

Rodgers added that McCarthy fell asleep multiple times in a recent quarterbacks meeting and missed some walkthroughs and other team meetings throughout the rest of the week.

Rodgers indicated that his benching and his ongoing issues with McCarthy marked the end of his time as the Steelers' starting quarterback, saying, "That ship has sailed. ... At this point, I'm not going back."

McCarthy and Rodgers have a prior relationship dating back to their days together with the Green Bay Packers, winning a Super Bowl in the 2010 season. In addition to their working relationship deteriorating, Rodgers said the coach did things that made him concerned about his health, such as breaking down two halftime meetings in Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles by saying, "1-2-3 Packers."

"It began as a concerned friend. … If you're falling asleep in meetings, you're unhealthy," Rodgers said .

According to ESPN's Brooke Pryor , "Multiple league sources corroborated Rodgers' account to ESPN. One source texted: 'It's all true.' Another source told ESPN that McCarthy 'crossed' Rodgers, leading to the quarterback's account Wednesday."

Rodgers went on to reveal that he's voiced his concerns to McCarthy directly, saying that this has been a conversation for "weeks and weeks." He said he also expressed his desire to take over the offensive play-calling, but he knew that McCarthy wouldn't want him to do that. They instead discussed QBs coach Tom Arth handling the play-calling, but McCarthy later changed his mind.

"We don't have to tell anybody. You're on the headset, Tom's on the headset, whatever we do, call the plays in, yeah we're good," he said . "Then I circled back later in the day and obviously that was not what the sentiment was as far as what we were doing moving forward."

The conversation over play-calling got so contentious that Rodgers said he told McCarthy, "If you don't change the play-calling or if you bench me, you should release me."

While all of this is only now coming to the surface, Rodgers said the whole Steelers organization is aware of McCarthy's behavior. He added that while he initially vouched for McCarthy, he admits that he was wrong.

"This isn't what I signed up for. … I vouched for him to [general manager] Omar [Khan] that he should get an interview," Rodgers said. "I am not a victim. I'm accountable."

Rodgers was asked why he chose to reunite with McCarthy if they still had issues dating back to their days with the Packers.

"It's on me because I vouched for him and I had the hope it was going to be different. There's no way. He knows it's my last year, he knows it's his dream job, he's back in his hometown. It's going to be different," he responded .

During all the hubbub surrounding Rodgers, many Steelers teammates declined to speak to reporters in Wednesday's open locker room session.

The Steelers announced on Tuesday that Rodgers will be inactive on Black Friday, while veteran backup Mason Rudolph will take over as the starter against the Broncos:

Rodgers, who turns 43 next Wednesday, re-signed with Pittsburgh on a one-year deal this past offseason. He previously announced that the 2026 campaign would be his 22nd and final season in the NFL.

Through 10 games, Rodgers threw for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions to help lead the Steelers to a 6-4 record. However, the team's offense has struggled mightily in back-to-back losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles, failing to reach the 20-point mark in either game.

In addition to this week's Black Friday game against the Broncos, the Steelers will be featured in upcoming national broadcasts against the Houston Texans on Sunday Night Football and the Jacksonville Jaguars on Monday Night Football in Weeks 13 and 14, respectively. Besides Rudolph, second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar are Pittsburgh's other quarterback options.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk, Jayden Daniels' Updated Fantasy Outlook for Commanders After WR's Contract
articles.summary: It took longer to arrive than originally anticipated, but the outcome everyone expected back in the offseason with Brandon Aiyuk joining the Washington Commanders is finally a reality.
articles.body:
It took longer to arrive than originally anticipated, but the outcome everyone expected back in the offseason with Brandon Aiyuk joining the Washington Commanders is finally a reality.

Aiyuk' agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN's Adam Schefter that the veteran wide receiver is signing with the Commanders to join their practice squad.

While there will be plenty of talk about the reunion between Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels from their one season together in college at Arizona State in 2019, the fantasy impact for this season is unlikely to be significant.

PFF's Nathan Jahnke noted in a best-case scenario Aiyuk could eventually work his way up to become the No. 3 receiver in Washington's offense if he ends up being elevated from the practice squad.

Daniels' fantasy value is no impacted at all by this news. He is tied for eighth among all quarterbacks in fantasy points per game this season despite playing without No. 1 target Terry McLaurin since Week 6 when he suffered a torn patellar tendon.

Making that level of play even more impressive is Daniels hasn't been as successful running the ball this season as he was in the previous two years. Monday's win over the Cincinnati Bengals was his first time with more than 30 yards on the ground since Week 5.

From a pure fantasy standpoint, we have no idea how long it might take Aiyuk before he will get elevated from the practice squad.

It's safe to assume it won't happen for the Commanders' next game on Sunday, so the earliest would be Week 13. That gives Aiyuk two weeks to show he can make any sort of impact before most fantasy leagues start the playoffs in Week 15.

One of the things that got lost in all of the Aiyuk discussion during his falling out with the San Francisco 49ers and wait for him to get released is he hasn't played in a game in more than two full calendar years.

Aiyuk's last appearance was on Oct. 20, 2024, when he tore his ACL, MCL and meniscus in a game against the Kansas City Chiefs. No one has any idea what he's going to look like in a game and how much of his previous ability he still possesses until he is back on the field.

Even before the injury during that season, Aiyuk had started to show signs of decline from his All-Pro year in 2023. He had a 10.7 percent drop rate on 45 targets and 1.74 yards per route run, down from 3.02 in 2023 and 1.91 in 2022.

Unless you're in a deep fantasy league with at least 20 teams and your receiver room has been depleted with injuries, Aiyuk is unlikely to be an upgrade this season.

If the Commanders give Aiyuk meaningful reps, he is absolutely worth keeping an eye in 2027 when he will be going into his age-29 season.

Aaron Rodgers said he had played his last game for the Pittsburgh Steelers in an appearance on ESPN's Pat McAfee Show shortly before NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported he was being waived.

Rodgers told McAfee Wednesday the "ship has sailed" on his potential return to the Steelers.

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette 's Gerry Dulac also reported the Steelers' decision to waive Rodgers was "hastened" by Rodgers' appearance on McAfee's show.

The Steelers had announced Tuesday night Rodgers would be inactive for Friday's matchup against the Denver Broncos.

Rodgers told McAfee the Steelers made that move because he had offered the team an "ultimatum" when pushing for McCarthy to step down as play caller.

The quarterback had $8.5 million in remaining base salary at the time of his release, per Spotrac , although ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted the interview could be seen as "conduct detrimental to the team."

CBS Sports' Joel Corry noted the maximum penalty Rodgers could receive for that contact would be $6.1 million. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported his "understanding is there could be money voided" and the Steelers still "have to work through that."

Rodgers said Wednesday his split with McCarthy had stemmed from concerns regarding the head coach's health.

"You're gonna release me? Cool," Rodgers said. "You're gonna deflect this thing, and make it that you were trying to bench me, and that I'm at home contemplating whether or not I'm going to accept a benching? Couldn't be farther from the truth. That word never came up in our meetings."

He continued, "It wasn't a veiled ultimatum. It wasn't posturing... to tell him that what's best for the team is for him to not call the plays, and if he wasn't up for that, then they should probably release me."

Rodgers claimed McCarthy had slept through meetings, accidentally referred to his team as the Packers when breaking a halftime huddle against the Philadelphia Eagles, and wasn't prepared as of Tuesday for the Steelers' Friday game against the visiting Denver Broncos.

"This has been a conversation for weeks... and every time I bring these things up, he denies it," Rodgers said.

Rodgers said he participated in Tuesday's walkthrough with the expectation he would be starting Friday, but that his status changed after another evening meeting with McCarthy.

The Steelers brought McCarthy in on a five-year deal ahead of the 2026 season, which Rodgers said was "on me because I vouched for him" this offseason.

articles.body:
At least one legendary Pittsburgh Steelers player is backing up Aaron Rodgers.

Rodgers made waves Wednesday during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show when he revealed he would not be returning to the Steelers. What's more, he said head coach Mike McCarthy was "snoring" in team meetings (h/t ESPN ).

"Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting," Rodgers said. "Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened."

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

James Harrison said on social media it was "not the first time" he had heard similar things:

That wasn't all Rodgers said about McCarthy.

He revealed the head coach said in the locker room during Pittsburgh's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, "All right, one, two, three Packers."

McCarthy and Rodgers used to be together on the Green Bay Packers, although the coach was last there during the 2018 season and has since coached the Dallas Cowboys as well.

Rodgers also said he learned he was being benched from teammate Pat Freiermuth and still hasn't heard from McCarthy.

This is McCarthy's first season as the head coach of the Steelers. There has never been any overlap between him and Harrison, who played for Pittsburgh from 2002 until 2017 as one of the most iconic defenders in franchise history.

His resume includes two Super Bowl titles, a Defensive Player of the Year, two First Team All-Pro nods and five Pro Bowl selections. While he hasn't played in the NFL since the 2017 campaign, it is not a stretch to assume he still has connections within the Steelers organization.

He suggested he has heard things similar to what Rodgers was saying Wednesday, which only adds to the storylines ahead of Pittsburgh's game against the Denver Broncos on Friday.

articles.title: Derrick Henry Injured, Latest Updates on Concussion Recovery Ahead of Ravens vs. Texans
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter provided an update on Derrick Henry Wednesday after the star running back was placed in the concussion protocol following Sunday's 35-32 loss against the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter provided an update on Derrick Henry Wednesday after the star running back was placed in the concussion protocol following Sunday's 35-32 loss against the Carolina Panthers.

"Derrick had a couple of brief symptoms of a concussion right towards the end of that game. Tested clear. Put him back in protocol just to kind of really make sure," he told reporters. "So when the [practice report] comes out today, he would have been limited. We do expect him to be back, obviously."

Henry, 32, rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's loss against Carolina, adding four catches for 17 yards. For the season he's rushed for 793 yards and 11 touchdowns and is well on his way to a fifth straight 1,000-yard season and the eighth of his career overall.

He's also caught 21 passes for 102 yards and a touchdown this season.

While Henry has continued to do his thing, the Ravens are reeling with quarterback Lamar Jackson out with a broken and dislocated thumb (and previously out with an ankle issue). Baltimore has now lost six straight games, has fallen to 4-7 on the season and has season their playoff hopes all but extinguished.

The hope was that acquiring Jacoby Brissett would help salvage a floundering season, but in two games the veteran quarterback has thrown for 616 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, taking four sacks.

A healthy does of Henry is probably the team's best chance at offensive consistency at this point. For now, it sounds like he'll be available for the team's matchup against the Houston Texans on Sunday.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Released by Steelers After Explosive Comments About Mike McCarthy, Benching
articles.summary: In a surprising end to the likely final chapter of his Hall of Fame career, Pittsburgh Steelers veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers has been released.
articles.body:
In a surprising end to the likely final chapter of his Hall of Fame career, Pittsburgh Steelers veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers has been released.

The Steelers benched Rodgers ahead of Friday's game against the Denver Broncos and replaced him with veteran backup Mason Rudolph. Rodgers led Pittsburgh to a 6-4 record, throwing for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions.

Rodgers' release comes hours after he appeared on Wednesday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show and completely ripped Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, alleging that he exhibited questionable behavior, such as falling asleep in team meetings.

Rodgers will be subject to waivers and can be claimed at any time up until 4 pm ET tomorrow. He would become an unrestricted free agent if he clears waivers.

NFL insider Dianna Russini reported on Wednesday's episode of The Russini Report that Rodgers likely won't garner much interest if he hits the open market.

"And what if Rodgers were to get released? Could he sign with a contender whose starter gets hurt? From what I sense, I don't think there's gonna be a big market, but you never know," Russini said .

Rodgers, who will turn 43 on Dec. 2, said after re-signing with Pittsburgh that the 2026 season would likely be his last in the NFL. The 22-year veteran appeared to maintain his status as a reliable starter when the Steelers opened the year with a 6-2 record, but their offensive struggles in back-to-back losses led to his benching in Week 11.

It didn't take long for Rodgers to voice his side of the story, telling McAfee that his relationship with McCarthy had completely deteriorated, with issues dating back to their time with the Green Bay Packers. The two of them had multiple disagreements over play-calling and McCarthy's approach to the team.

A one-time Super Bowl champion, Rodgers is widely regarded as one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time. The four-time NFL MVP owns multiple league records and earned 10 Pro Bowl selections. He ranks third all-time with 543 passing touchdowns and fifth with 68,515 passing yards.

If Rodgers officially ends his career, his disappointing tenures with the Steelers and New York Jets will be hard to overlook. However, he is a sure-fire Hall of Famer who will be remembered as one of the best passers the league has ever seen.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers released by Steelers after benching, comments on 'Pat McAfee Show'
articles.summary: Rodgers announced in May that the 2026 season would be his last in the NFL.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers' time with the Pittsburgh Steelers has come to an end following his benching and comments on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show."

The Steelers announced on Wednesday afternoon that the 43-year-old quarterback has been released.

The situation went from the Steelers announcing late Tuesday evening that Rodgers would be benched to him airing his feelings about head coach Mike McCarthy less than 24 hours later.

On "McAfee," Rodgers claimed that McCarthy fell asleep and snored during a quarterbacks meeting after arriving late. He also said the Steelers head coach broke down the team during halftime of Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles by saying, "Alright, 1-2-3-Packers!"

The four-time NFL MVP added that he found out he was being benched in favor of Mason Rudolph from Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth.

"I was talking to Muth and a couple of the guys, and he said, 'I can't believe they're doing this.' And I said, 'Doing what?' I didn't know," Rodgers said. "And he told me, and obviously, there had been a lot of things in motion at that point. I didn't hear from Mike [McCarthy]."

"Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, and that word [benching] never came up."

What comes next for Rodgers? That's to be determined. He said on "McAfee" that the "ship has sailed" in regards to a return to the Steelers. Now, he will be free agent once he clears waivers.

Rodgers announced in May that the 2026 season would be his last in the NFL.

In 10 games this season, Rodgers has thrown for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and 6 interceptions.

articles.title: Panthers Burn IR Slot Despite Christensen Being Healthy
articles.summary: The Panthers let Brady Christensen's window expire, ending his 2026 season and wasting a roster slot despite him being fully ready to play.
articles.body:
They let the 21-day practice window for offensive lineman Brady Christensen expire on Tuesday. This decision ended his 2026 season early even though he is physically ready to play. The team chose to keep him off the active roster, a choice that burns a valuable resource for the front office.

Head coach Dave Canales did not hide the fact that Christensen is fit to play. When the team opened the window in November, Canales stated, "He's healthy, he's strong, he's fit, he's ready to go." The offensive lineman has practiced in full for weeks after suffering a hamstring injury back in August. Despite this readiness, the Panthers did not activate him to the 53-man roster before the deadline. Instead, he reverts to injured reserve and his season is officially over.

The coach admitted the team wanted to see him play football to evaluate his fit. "But we've got to get some football under his belt here, so that'll be a good addition to the group to evaluate where you can help us potentially." Waiting for a player to get game reps is a valid strategy. The team now has a player who cannot help them in the immediate future.

The real cost of this decision goes beyond just losing a player for a few weeks. Designating Christensen as a return candidate means the Panthers still count that move against their injured reserve return limit. The team wasted one of its IR return slots even though he never got activated.

According to ProFootballTalk , Christensen stays on injured reserve and cannot rejoin the 2026 team roster. He is a third-round pick from 2021 with 59 career games and 34 starts to his name. A torn Achilles during the 2025 season and a hamstring problem in August have affected him. They also know he is healthy right now.

Canales called the choice difficult during a press conference on Friday. "It's a difficult decision. That's something Dan and I have been talking about and working through, especially with what Brady has done for us. The Panthers think current roster options surpass Christensen. That is the reason given for the move. The team plays the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30, at 8:15 p.m. ET at Raymond James Stadium.

articles.title: Rhamondre Stevenson sets record straight on speedy injury comeback
articles.summary: Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson suffered a knee injury in the loss to the Packers that was reportedly set to sideline him for a few weeks.
articles.body:
Injuries have not been kind to the New England Patriots this season, and in the team's blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers, they lost one of their top offensive weapons.

Rhamondre Stevenson suffered a knee injury, with multiple reports implying that the running back would be sidelined for a few weeks. So, imagine the surprise when Stevenson not only was spotted with the team the next week in Germany, but also took part in practice as a limited participant.

And he didn't stop there, with Stevenson being listed as active for the game.

He went from a possible injured reserve candidate to not missing a single game. So, what went into that?

"A bunch of recovery," Stevenson told Patriots Wire in an exclusive interview. "(The trainers) did a good job of just getting me available again... Leg wasn't feeling 100 percent, but I was well enough to go out there and participate with the team and try to help them out a little bit."

However, he did admit that based on what he was initially told, his speedy return to the field came as a bit of a surprise.

"Yeah, honestly, yes," he explained. "It was great. If I could help my team in any way possible, I want to do that. So, I wasn't 100 percent, obviously, but if I could go out there and be healthy enough to participate, like I said, that's what I'm going to do every week."

But, while the media was saying a couple weeks, he didn't think it would take that long.

"First and foremost, probably the media and what they're saying isn't always true," Stevenson said. "But I think it just attests to how tough we are, how willing we're trying to be out there with our team, and just trying to be available for our teammates."

The running back was also asked if he felt 100 percent after the bye, but Stevenson chose to keep that information to himself. So, while he may not have been ready to reveal exactly where he stands physically, one thing is clear: He's willing to do whatever it takes to be on the field for his teammates.

Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook .

articles.summary: Five Minnesota Vikings players will be listed as non-participants after Wednesday's walkthrough. Here's what you need to know.
articles.body:
Christian Darrisaw left Sunday night's game in Mexico City twice. The Minnesota Vikings' left tackle went to the sideline with a shoulder injury in the first half, came back after halftime and was ruled out in the fourth quarter of their 35-10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

Now, after dropping three of their last four, the Vikings are 7-3 and looking to turn the momentum back in their favor Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons (3-7), who have lost three straight and are coming off their bye week.

MN Vikings hold five players out of Wednesday's walkthrough

Wednesday's practice was just a walkthrough, but Kevin O'Connell said Darrisaw, Harrison Smith, Jordan Addison, Isaiah Rodgers and Jalen Redmond were all estimated non-participants.

The Vikings will hold a walk-through instead of a practice today, but Christian Darrisaw, Harrison Smith, Jordan Addison, Isaiah Rodgers and Jalen Redmond will be estimated as non-participants, Kevin O'Connell said. — Ben Goessling (@BenGoessling) November 25, 2026

KOC said the Vikings will have full practices Thursday and Friday, and seemed hopeful that most of the DNP's from Wednesday will be ready to roll by Sunday: "Guys are kind of working through things with the intent and the hope of maybe seeing where they can get to by the end of the week."

Christian Darrisaw's shoulder is day to day

This isn't the first shoulder issue Darrisaw has dealt with this month. He hurt his other shoulder in the Nov. 1 loss at Detroit and was limited in practice that week, but still played against the Buffalo Bills that Monday.

On Wednesday, O'Connell was whether he was confident that Darrisaw will play Sunday against Atlanta. If nothing else, it appears the injury is not longterm.

"Yeah, I think it's early. It's early to tell right now one way or the other, but I would say we definitely don't have long-term fears of this. And it's something that we're kind of dealing with day to day." Kevin O'Connell – Minnesota Vikings

"Yeah, I think it's early. It's early to tell right now one way or the other, but I would say we definitely don't have long-term fears of this. And it's something that we're kind of dealing with day to day."

Darrisaw has played in nine of Minnesota's 10 games this season. The only one he missed was the Oct. 11 game at New Orleans, where Ryan Van Demark played all 71 offensive snaps at left tackle in a 23-13 win.

Against the 49ers, Darrisaw had an 89.8 pass-blocking grade from PFF and didn't allow a pressure on 28 pass-blocking snaps. Van Demark, who replaced him, had a 21.2 pass-blocking grade and gave up three pressures on 19 pass-blocking snaps.

Where Harrison Smith and the other three Vikings stand

Nobody reported an in-game injury for Smith against San Francisco. When a reporter asked whether the veteran safety had an injury or a vet rest day, O'Connell said:

"He had a little soreness coming out of the game, but yeah … I think if you asked him, he probably does most, most days, so he'll work through it and we'll see where he's at, but very hopeful on Harry." Kevin O'Connell – Minnesota Vikings

"He had a little soreness coming out of the game, but yeah … I think if you asked him, he probably does most, most days, so he'll work through it and we'll see where he's at, but very hopeful on Harry."

Smith has played in all 10 games this season, with 21 tackles , half a sack, two interceptions and five passes defensed. Redmond is dealing with an ankle injury, Kevin Seifert (ESPN) reported .

The defensive lineman has also played in all 10 games, with 32 tackles , two sacks, 6.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and four passes defensed. He had four tackles, two for loss, against San Francisco.

Isaiah Rodgers has a quad injury. The cornerback was added to the injury report on Nov. 19, was limited the last two days at practice last week, then was made inactive against the 49ers. In nine games, Rodgers has 29 tackles , an interception, a fumble recovery and five passes defensed.

Addison has missed the last two games with a thumb injury he suffered in practice on Nov. 13. He had surgery three days later, and O'Connell said Nov. 18 that the receiver will not go on short-term injured reserve for now.

On Monday, O'Connell said he doesn't "necessarily expect to have him this week," but that Addison is "progressing really well for having just gotten that thing fixed." Addison has 18 catches for 277 yards and a touchdown in seven games this season.

articles.title: ‘Don’t fall for that’ – Tom Brady says he never believed Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce claim
articles.summary: Travis Kelce scored two touchdowns in the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 11 win over the Arizona Cardinals. NFL legend Tom Brady has given his thoughts on Patrick...
articles.body:
Travis Kelce scored two touchdowns in the Kansas City Chiefs' Week 11 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

NFL legend Tom Brady has given his thoughts on Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce's evergreen connection.

Brady told his Fox Sports Power Rankings segment that he cannot believe anybody doubted the endurance of the connection between Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce.

Despite Mahomes coming off an ACL injury and Kelce having to bat off retirement rumors at this stage of his career, Brady is adamant the pairing is still 'elite'.

Brady said: "He hasn't thrown a pick in a month. KC's won three in a row. And you guys tried to tell me Mahomes-to-Kelce wasn't an elite connection anymore… don't fall for that."

The former Patriots quarterback then issued a detailed explanation of how Mahomes and Kelce keep doing it, despite the league having a decade's worth of game tape on them.

He explained that they know each other so well that they can rely on their instincts and are able to quickly adapt to situations.

Brady said: "They have a connection that's both verbal and non-verbal, and they always have the ability with the route concepts to adapt in the moment, too.

"So Travis knows, let's say he's breaking out and there's somebody out there, he knows that he can stem out and, with his body language, turn back in and Pat can fit it on his inside shoulder, and vice versa if they're inside.

"So there's still a lot of route adaptation. As long as Travis knows the concept of the route and knows where other guys are, he knows which confined spaces he can work his way open to."

Travis Kelce overtook Brady's former teammate Rob Gronkowski at the weekend for career receiving touchdowns.

Together, Mahomes and Kelce recently broke the NFL record for the most career regular-season passing and receiving yards by a quarterback–tight end duo.

Earlier this month against the Jets, the Chiefs pair surpassed the previous mark of 9,360 yards held by Philip Rivers and Antonio Gates.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers rips Mike McCarthy, says Steelers coach fell asleep in meeting and mistakenly called team 'Packers'; other players reportedly corroborate quarterback's account
articles.summary: Rodgers appeared on the Pat McAfee Show after the team announced his benching Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers did not stay silent for long following his surprise benching . And shortly after Rodgers publicly accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of everything from sleeping in meetings to mistakenly calling the team the "Packers," the franchise reportedly decided to release the veteran quarterback .

Rodgers, a four-time NFL MVP, joined the "Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday afternoon to address his benching … and he did not hold back when it came to sharing his side of how the events of the week unfolded — or when it comes to his feelings about McCarthy.

"I found out that I was gonna be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth," Rodgers said in the interview. "I was talking to Muth and a couple of the guys, and he said, 'I can't believe they're doing this.' And I said, 'Doing what?' I didn't know. And he told me, and obviously, there had been a lot of things in motion at that point. I didn't hear from Mike [McCarthy].

"Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, and that word [benching] never came up," Rodgers continued.

After that, Rodgers released a windfall of scathing accusations against McCarthy, ripping into his head coach for a series of events over the past week that "ultimately led to where we're at now."

Rodgers highlights bizarre sequence of events with McCarthy leading up to benching

Rodgers said McCarthy arrived late to a quarterbacks' meeting last Wednesday, in which the coach fell asleep and was snoring.

"Last Wednesday, we're in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rogers said. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. Less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened."

Rodgers accused McCarthy of missing an offensive meeting the following day and also missed the Friday walkthrough.

"Doesn't come to the first walkthrough," Rodgers said. "Doesn't come to the protection walkthrough on Thursday. Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don't have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly. And then comes Sunday, when obviously we struggled, and the product wasn't great."

'Mike [McCarthy] didn't want to get to know the defense'

Rodgers also ripped into McCarthy's relationships with players on the team, alleging that he didn't care to get to know the defense and had lost many of those players well before the end.

"There were some guys early on that were … didn't like the way things were going, especially defensive guys. Mike didn't want to get to know the defense," Rodgers said. "At one point, I told him, 'You should really lean into the defensive guys a little bit more and talk to those guys,' and he said, 'Well, I don't think I need to.' And I said, 'Well, I disagree with that.'

"He already kind of lost a lot of those guys, and I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was, at halftime, toward the end of it … he says, 'Alright, 1-2-3-Packers!' That's what he broke it down on in the locker room," Rodgers said. "We all looked around, going, 'What the f***? What is going on? Where's his head at, at this point?"

The Steelers went on to lose that game, 19-16, snapping a seven-game losing streak for the Philadelphia Eagles. Rodgers took five sacks in the loss, completing 30-of-44 pass attempts for 227 yards and a score.

Rodgers hits his breaking point with McCarthy

Clearly, the loss was a tipping point for Rodgers.

"I went in on Monday, and I just said, 'Hey, this last week, this is not what we talked about.' We've had these conversations for months now. And it began as a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy. If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy. If you're not coming to everything you should be coming to as a playcaller, [you're unhealthy].

"I mean, how many quarterbacks around the league are dealing with the same type of stuff? I gave you one week. I could go week-by-week throughout the season on stuff that was going on.

"Monday, we're having this conversation, and I said, 'We need to make a change for the betterment of the team.'"

The change Rodgers was hoping for was a change in playcaller. But instead, the team made a change at quarterback.

Rogers said he confronted McCarthy about his 'habits'

"I felt like I was talking to him at the behest of the team," Rogers said. "It was pretty wild. I'm saying these things to him that I told you. He's denying all of it. He's denying sleeping. I go, 'Mike, there's five guys in the room that would sign an affidavit.' There's no hyperbole. There's no trying to stick it you. What's best for the team is you give [play calling] up to somebody, you take care of yourself, you take care of your health, do the schedule and do the team meetings and let that be that."

Rodgers said McCarthy doesn't watch film

"When I talk to him on Tuesdays, he says I haven't seen the film yet, I haven't seen the film." Rodgers said. "I don't know how that's possible on Tuesday when you play on a Sunday. That part's disrespectful to the game. You have peoples' livelihoods involved, players and coaches."

Rodgers said he told McCarthy to release him if benched him

"I left it with him that if you try and bench me or don't change the play-calling, then you should just release me because I feel like at this point I'm doing what's right for the organization," Rogers said. "He responded with, 'I'm going to do what's right for the organization,' and, in his mind, that's getting rid of me."

Rodgers said 'ship has sailed' on a return to the Steelers

How do Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers move forward after this?

Well … apparently, they don't. Rodgers acknowledged as much nearing the end of his McAfee appearance, saying the "ship has sailed" on a return to the team. Soon after Rodgers' interview concluded, it was reported that the Steelers were releasing Rodgers , according to Pittsburgh Post-Gazette beat writer Gerry Dulac. Other reports have since confirmed the same.

The real question now is how the Steelers will move forward with McCarthy, after multiple league sources have corroborated Rodgers' account to ESPN.

articles.title: Lions place Skyler Gill-Howard on IR, elevate DE from practice squad
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions have placed Skyler Gill-Howard on IR, while bringing up another DL from the practice squad.
articles.body:
As expected, the Detroit Lions have placed rookie defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard on injured reserve, ending his 2026 season. Earlier this week, Lions coach Dan Campbell indicated that Gill-Howard suffered a knee injury during a late fourth quarter goal line play, and he will require surgery to repair the damage.

"I hate that for him. And he's had a heck of a season up to this point," Campbell said.

Gill-Howard appeared in all 10 Lions games this season, holding a significant role as a pass rusher and disrupter in the run game. Despite being a sixth-round pick, Gill-Howard worked his way up and played 316 snaps—fifth among defensive lineman in Detroit this season.

Gill-Howard is the third Lions defender to be placed on injured reserve in the last four weeks, joining linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) and Aidan Hutchinson (torn ACL).

In his place, the Lions will rely upon the likes of Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams, Tyler Lacy, and Levi Onwuzurike to step up in his place. They could also play Mekhi Wingo, who shares a lot of physical traits with Gill-Howard, but hasn't been active for a single game yet this season.

The Lions did not immediately fill Gill-Howard's spot on the 53-man roster, but they did temporarily elevate defensive end Anthony Lucas from the practice squad for Thursday's game against the Chicago Bears. This is the second time Lucas has been elevated, playing in 12 defensive snaps against the Miami Dolphins a few weeks ago. Lucas is an undrafted rookie out of USC who brings a ton of intriguing athletic traits, but is still growing as a defender.

articles.title: Broncos injury report: Sai'vion Jones and Taylor Rapp updates
articles.summary: The Broncos wrapped up their practice week on Wednesday ahead of a Black Friday showdown with the Steelers. They will travel tonight.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos are in relatively good health going into a Black Friday showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 12.

Defensive linemen practiced indoors on Wednesday, so there's no word yet on the status of defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones ( hamstring ), but safety Taylor Rapp ( quadriceps ) was present for the portion of Wednesday's practice open to media members. Rapp was limited on Tuesday. Meanwhile, running back J.K. Dobbins ( suspended ) remains away from the facility.

If Jones is not able to play in Pittsburgh, Denver's remaining defensive linemen would be Zach Allen, D.J. Jones, Malcolm Roach, Jordan Jackson and rookie Tyler Onyedim . The Broncos also brought in four free agent defensive linemen for tryouts on Tuesday.

As for the Steelers, linebacker Alex Highsmith (ankle) appears unlikely to play against Denver. Highsmith would be a notable absence for Pittsburgh as his 5.5 sacks rank second on the team behind T.J. Watt (7.5 sacks).

The Broncos and Steelers will announce their final injury reports with game statuses on Thursday.

articles.title: Detroit Lions rule CB out, list two starters questionable vs. Bears
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions ruled one of their defensive backs out, and listed two players as questionable against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions (8-2) released their Wednesday game status report ahead of their Thanksgiving showdown against the Chicago Bears (8-2).

Lions head coach Dan Campbell announced on Tuesday that rookie defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard had suffered a season-ending knee injury . Naturally, Gill-Howard was listed out on the game status report.

Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. was also ruled out with a shoulder injury. Rakestraw has played in seven games this season, starting one. The 5-foot-11, 192-pound corner has registered 11 tackles, two pass breakups and one forced fumble this season.

Starting safety Chuck Clark (hamstring) and EDGE DJ Wonnum (back) were both listed as questionable.

Clark leads the Lions with 61 tackles. The 6-foot, 210-pound veteran safety has also tallied four passes defensed, two interceptions, two forced fumbles, two sacks, and two tackles for loss.

Wonnum has started four games this season, totaling 24 tackles and a team-leading seven sacks and eight tackles for loss.

Rakestraw, a 2024 second-round pick out of Missouri, entered the 2026 NFL season having played in just eight NFL games as he's battled hamstring and shoulder injuries throughout his career. All of those eight games played before 2026 were during his rookie season in 2024.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers became the NFL's rebel, and his scorched-earth interview was a fitting end in Pittsburgh
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers delivered an interview that will be remembered for many years.
articles.body:
Near the end of an instantly legendary interview, which will be remembered for years and years to come, Aaron Rodgers felt the need to explain why he just had aired out Mike McCarthy in a way that a player has never quite ripped his coach before.

The way Rodgers delivered the message on "The Pat McAfee Show" was almost as startling as the accusations themselves. He said McCarthy would sleep in meetings and miss practices. That he didn't bother to get to know some Steelers defensive stars like Cameron Heyward and T.J. Watt at all. And Rodgers told it all without ever getting emotional. He rarely changed his matter-of-fact tone over the more than 30 minutes the interview lasted.

He then needed to tell everyone why he was spilling all the embarrassing stories, or more specifically, why he didn't care about the fallout.

"It's going to be hard for [other Steelers teammates] to tell the truth, like I can," Rodgers told McAfee. "I can, because what are the repercussions for me? I don't care about getting released. I don't care about making any more money. I don't care how this is viewed by the same people who railed me for COVID who already have their opinions about me. I'm standing on the truth. That's why it's not emotional for me anymore."

Everyone already knew that, at the age of 42, Rodgers didn't really care what people thought of him anymore. Multiple interviews on multiple topics late in his career are proof of that. And there should certainly be skepticism over what the truth actually is. Disgruntled parties can twist stories to fit self-serving narratives , and Rodgers had just been benched for the first time in his 22-year NFL career. He was released not long after the McAfee interview, which was no surprise to anyone who heard it.

The nuance of what Rodgers said doesn't matter much to this larger point: The defiant reputation Rodgers grew late in his career was always going to lead to a moment like this, which has never really been seen in the NFL before.

When word started getting around that Rodgers was going on McAfee's ESPN show at about 1:40 p.m. Eastern time, it was time to tune in. There was no chance that Rodgers was going to go on a show that he has been on many times before and acquiesce. Everyone knew he was incapable of going out quietly. And he didn't.

Even with that as a backdrop, it was shocking. Many things that happen in a meeting or locker room do not get shared with the public. Rodgers revealed it all, or at least his version of it.

Rodgers said he found out he was benched when tight end Pat Freiermuth called him incredulous about the news Rodgers hadn't heard yet. That ended up being one of the tamer revelations of the interview with McAfee.

Rodgers said that last week, McCarthy fell asleep twice in a quarterback meeting on Wednesday. Rodgers said McCarthy also missed an offensive meeting and a walkthrough on Thursday, then missed another walkthrough on Friday and missed a morning meeting on Saturday. There was no team meeting "for whatever reason" on Saturday night, Rodgers said.

"Last Wednesday we were in a quarterback meeting, Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rodgers said. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we all looked around, five minutes later you heard the snoring again."

Rodgers wouldn't stop. He said McCarthy told him on Tuesday that he was behind in watching film on the Broncos, who the Steelers play on Sunday.

"He just says, this is Tuesday by the way, three days from playing, he says "I'm a little behind on film, I've just seen clips at this point,'" Rodgers said. "There's already a first and second, third down install in at this point. That's when I'm like, what are we doing?"

He said it was common for McCarthy to tell him he had not watched film.

"I don't think he knows the plan. I think he learns the plan during the week," Rodgers told McAfee. "Multiple times he said he doesn't watch film, when I've talked to him on Tuesdays, he hasn't seen the film yet. I don't know how that's possible, on a Tuesday after you play on a Sunday. That's the whole point. That part is disrespectful to the game itself, but you have peoples' careers involved."

Rodgers said the issues had been going on for weeks in Pittsburgh, and years before that when the two were together with the Green Bay Packers. He went so far as to take responsibility for suggesting to the Steelers that McCarthy should get an interview after Mike Tomlin stepped down as head coach, because he knew McCarthy's habits. Rodgers went back years, talking about similar situations with the Packers, particularly after an NFC championship game loss at Seattle at the end of the 2014 season in which he confronted McCarthy about his "habits that week" including missing multiple walkthroughs and meetings.

Story after story came from Rodgers, who offered them up with the same amount of emotion as if he was reading a grocery list.

"I've sat on this for a long time," Rodgers said. "I sat on it for 10 years, 10 years in Green Bay with this stuff going on, 10 years that I was aware of. But we worked around it. We won division championships, went to the playoffs eight straight years. It's like, is there a better way to do this? Is there a world where this doesn't exist like this? It's on me, because I vouched for him, and I thought it would be different."

Many things have and will be said about Rodgers, but it's also true to say that no other player would have given an interview quite like that one.

The beginning of the end of Rodgers' time in Pittsburgh came when he went to McCarthy with what he called an ultimatum. McCarthy should give up play-calling, or release him.

"It wasn't a veiled ultimatum," Rodger said. "It wasn't posturing."

The end of his time with the Steelers officially came shortly after an interview that will be infamous in NFL circles. If Rodgers was angling to get released and perhaps finish what he said will be his final season starting somewhere else, he knew how to do it.

There haven't been many NFL situations to play out this way in the public realm. Rodgers' interview that led to his release will go alongside Terrell Owens doing pushups in his driveway, Antonio Brown quitting on the Buccaneers and running back to the locker room in the middle of a game or any other infamous moments that won't be forgotten. There's a code that many of the things Rodgers shared aren't to be repeated in the media . He clearly didn't care because he shared it all, or at least his version of what happened.

There will be a fallout from it as Rodgers walks away from the fire he set. McCarthy's reputation will be hard to repair after this, and perhaps that was Rodgers' goal after being benched in an unceremonious way near the end of what he said will be his final season. Perhaps players will leak confirmation to Rodgers' stories anonymously ( ("It's all true," one source told ESPN ), but not many people are willing to rip their boss on the record. But it will all linger over the Steelers as long as McCarthy is coaching there.

Rodgers didn't care. The breaking point for him, he said, came at halftime of last week's loss at Philadelphia when McCarthy brought the team together and broke them down with a "1, 2, 3, Packers!" McCarthy last coached the Packers in 2018.

"Eight years removed, with a team in between," Rodgers said. "And a game we needed to win to get to 7-3."

The breaking point for McCarthy and the Steelers might have been that he shared that story at all.

From the outside looking in, it had been a fun reunion between Rodgers and McCarthy, at least before this week. The Steelers had lost two in a row, but at 6-4 they are still in the playoff field. That's not what we'll remember. We'll remember the unbelievable way it all ended in a public manner over a period of about 14 hours.

"It had a chance, it really did," Rodgers said. "It had a good chance to be one of those really cool stories."

It did end up being a heck of a story, and while it would be cliche to say this is all not the story Rodgers wanted, that's only partially true. Given Rodgers' rebellious and outspoken ways the past few years, it almost certainly had to end like this.
